2.10.s:
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu teṣāṃ cikitsitam ..
vṛṣo nimba bṛhatyau ca guḍūcī ca samāṃsikā .. 1 ..
2.10.d:
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु तेषां चिकित्सितम् ॥
वृषो निम्ब बृहत्यौ च गुडूची च समांसिका ॥ 1 ॥
2.10.m: Puṣkara said: / Hereafter I shall declare their medical treatment; listen: / vṛṣa, nimba, the two bṛhatīs, guḍūcī, and māṃsī—

2.10.s:
śiṅghāṇakaharāpiṇḍī svedasya śirasastathā ..
yāvaśūkaṃ samadanaṃ pippalī viśvabheṣajam .. 2 ..
2.10.d:
शिङ्घाणकहरापिण्डी स्वेदस्य शिरसस्तथा ॥
यावशूकं समदनं पिप्पली विश्वभेषजम् ॥ 2 ॥
2.10.m: a paste of these destroys nasal discharge, as does sweating of the head. / Barley-alkali together with madana, long pepper, dried ginger,

2.10.s:
sarṣapā gṛhadhūmaśca nirguṇḍī surasā vacā ..
nimbapatrayutā pāyau vartiḥ śūlavināśinī .. 3 ..
2.10.d:
सर्षपा गृहधूमश्च निर्गुण्डी सुरसा वचा ॥
निम्बपत्रयुता पायौ वर्तिः शूलविनाशिनी ॥ 3 ॥
2.10.m: mustard seeds, chimney soot, nirguṇḍī, basil, and calamus, / combined with leaves of nimba, [made into] a suppository in the anus, destroys colic.

2.10.s:
hiṅgu puṣkaramūlaṃ ca nāgaraṃ sāmlavetasam ..
pippalī saindhavayutaṃ śūlaghnaṃ tūṣṇavāriṇā .. 4 ..
2.10.d:
हिङ्गु पुष्करमूलं च नागरं साम्लवेतसम् ॥
पिप्पली सैन्धवयुतं शूलघ्नं तूष्णवारिणा ॥ 4 ॥
2.10.m: Asafoetida, puṣkaramūla, ginger, together with amlavetasa, / long pepper, and rock salt, taken with warm water, destroys colic.

2.10.s:
nāgarātiviṣau mustā sānantā bilvamālakā ..
kvātho māsaṃ pibedvājī sarvātīsāranāśanam .. 5 ..
2.10.d:
नागरातिविषौ मुस्ता सानन्ता बिल्वमालका ॥
क्वाथो मासं पिबेद्वाजी सर्वातीसारनाशनम् ॥ 5 ॥
2.10.m: Ginger, ativiṣā, nut grass, together with anantā, wood-apple, and āmalaka— / a horse should drink this decoction for a month; it cures all dysenteries.

2.10.s:
priyaṃguśārivābhyāṃ ca yuktamājaṃ śṛtaṃ payaḥ ..
paryāptaśarkaraṃ pītvā śramādvājyavamucyate .. 6 ..
2.10.d:
प्रियंगुशारिवाभ्यां च युक्तमाजं शृतं पयः ॥
पर्याप्तशर्करं पीत्वा श्रमाद्वाज्यवमुच्यते ॥ 6 ॥
2.10.m: Boiled goat’s milk mixed with priyaṅgu and sarsaparilla, / having ample sugar—by drinking this, a horse is freed from exhaustion.

2.10.s:
droṇikāyāṃ tu dātavyā tailavastisturaṅgame ..
koṣṭhajāśca śirā vedhyāstena tasya sukhaṃ bhavet .. 7 ..
2.10.d:
द्रोणिकायां तु दातव्या तैलवस्तिस्तुरङ्गमे ॥
कोष्ठजाश्च शिरा वेध्यास्तेन तस्य सुखं भवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
2.10.m: An oil enema should be administered to a horse in a tub, / and veins arising in the abdomen should be punctured; thereby ease will come to him.

2.10.s:
dāḍimaṃ triphalāṃ vyoṣaṃ guḍaṃ ca samabhāgikam ..
piṇḍametatpradātavyamaśvānāṃ kāsanāśanam .. 8 ..
2.10.d:
दाडिमं त्रिफलां व्योषं गुडं च समभागिकम् ॥
पिण्डमेतत्प्रदातव्यमश्वानां कासनाशनम् ॥ 8 ॥
2.10.m: Pomegranate, the three fruits, the three spices, and jaggery in equal portions— / this bolus should be given; it cures cough in horses.

2.10.s:
priyaṅgurodhramadhubhiḥ pibanti sma rasaṃ hayāḥ ..
kṣīraṃ vāmaṃ ca kāloḍyaṃ kaśmalādvipramucyate .. 9 ..
2.10.d:
प्रियङ्गुरोध्रमधुभिः पिबन्ति स्म रसं हयाः ॥
क्षीरं वामं च कालोड्यं कश्मलाद्विप्रमुच्यते ॥ 9 ॥
2.10.m: Horses drank the juice with priyaṅgu, lodhra, and honey; / or [having drunk] raw milk properly stirred, [a horse] is freed from stupor.

2.10.s:
praskanneṣu ca sarveṣu śreya ādau viśoṣaṇam ..
abhyaṅgodvartanasnehanasyavartikramastataḥ .. 2.46.10 ..
2.10.d:
प्रस्कन्नेषु च सर्वेषु श्रेय आदौ विशोषणम् ॥
अभ्यङ्गोद्वर्तनस्नेहनस्यवर्तिक्रमस्ततः ॥ 2.46.10 ॥
2.10.m: In all prolapses, desiccation is first recommended; / then the sequence of anointing, rubbing, unction, errhine, and medicated wick.

2.10.s:
praskannaṃ praśamaṃ yāti yadi nānena karmaṇā ..
urasyupāntapārśve ca tato visrāvayecchirām .. 11 ..
2.10.d:
प्रस्कन्नं प्रशमं याति यदि नानेन कर्मणा ॥
उरस्युपान्तपार्श्वे च ततो विस्रावयेच्छिराम् ॥ 11 ॥
2.10.m: If prolapse is not pacified by this treatment, / one should then bleed a vein in the chest and near the flank.

2.10.s:
jvalitānāṃ turaṅgāṇāmayameva kriyākramaḥ ..
nasyamekaṃ vinā rāma sarvametatpraśasyate .. 12 ..
2.10.d:
ज्वलितानां तुरङ्गाणामयमेव क्रियाक्रमः ॥
नस्यमेकं विना राम सर्वमेतत्प्रशस्यते ॥ 12 ॥
2.10.m: This is the very course of treatment for feverish horses; / except for the errhine alone, O Rāma, all of this is commended.

2.10.s:
rodhrakarañjayormūlaṃ mātuluṅgāgnināgarāḥ ..
kuṣṭhahiṅguvacārāsnālepo'yaṃ śophanāśanaḥ .. 13 ..
2.10.d:
रोध्रकरञ्जयोर्मूलं मातुलुङ्गाग्निनागराः ॥
कुष्ठहिङ्गुवचारास्नालेपोऽयं शोफनाशनः ॥ 13 ॥
2.10.m: Roots of lodhra and karañja, citron, plumbago, and ginger; / this plaster of kuṣṭha, asafoetida, vacā, and rāsnā cures swelling.

2.10.s:
samāsena śirāṃ vidhyāddeyā vāpi jalaukasaḥ ..
tryahetryahe vā dharmajña nasyakarma samācaret .. 14 ..
2.10.d:
समासेन शिरां विध्याद्देया वापि जलौकसः ॥
त्र्यहेत्र्यहे वा धर्मज्ञ नस्यकर्म समाचरेत् ॥ 14 ॥
2.10.m: Briefly, one should pierce a vein, or leeches may also be applied; / or every three days, O knower of dharma, one should perform nasal administration.

2.10.s:
mañjiṣṭhā madhukaṃ drākṣā bṛhatyau raktacandanam ..
trapusībījamūlāni śṛṅgāṭakakaśerukam .. 15 ..
2.10.d:
मञ्जिष्ठा मधुकं द्राक्षा बृहत्यौ रक्तचन्दनम् ॥
त्रपुसीबीजमूलानि शृङ्गाटककशेरुकम् ॥ 15 ॥
2.10.m: Madder, liquorice, grape, the two bṛhatīs, red sandalwood, / seeds and roots of cucumber, water chestnut, and kaśeruka—

2.10.s:
ajāpayaḥ śṛtamidaṃ suśītaṃ śarkarānvitam..
pītvā niraśano vājī raktamehātpramucyate .. 16 ..
2.10.d:
अजापयः शृतमिदं सुशीतं शर्करान्वितम्॥
पीत्वा निरशनो वाजी रक्तमेहात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 16 ॥
2.10.m: this, boiled with goat's milk, well cooled, and mixed with sugar, / being drunk by a fasting horse, frees him from hematuria.

2.10.s:
manyāhanunigālasthaḥ śiraḥśopho galagraha ..
abhyaṅgaḥ kaṭutailena tatra teṣveva śasyate .. 17 ..
2.10.d:
मन्याहनुनिगालस्थः शिरःशोफो गलग्रह ॥
अभ्यङ्गः कटुतैलेन तत्र तेष्वेव शस्यते ॥ 17 ॥
2.10.m: For swelling of the head and throat spasms located in the nape, jaw, or throat, / massage with pungent oil is praised right there on those [spots].

2.10.s:
yavaiḥ snigdhakulatthaiśca tataḥ svedaṃ prayojayet ..
mṛdūkṛte tataḥ śophe nasyakarma samācaret ..18..
2.10.d:
यवैः स्निग्धकुलत्थैश्च ततः स्वेदं प्रयोजयेत् ॥
मृदूकृते ततः शोफे नस्यकर्म समाचरेत् ॥18॥
2.10.m: Then one should apply fomentation with barley and unctuous horsegram; / after the swelling has been softened, one should then perform nasal administration.

2.10.s:
vacā- - - - saindhavaṃ svaraso rasaḥ ..
kṛṣṇāhiṅuyutairebhiḥ kṛtvā nasyaṃ na sīdati ..19..
2.10.d:
वचा- - - - सैन्धवं स्वरसो रसः ॥
कृष्णाहिङुयुतैरेभिः कृत्वा नस्यं न सीदति ॥19॥
2.10.m: Vacā, [...], rock salt, fresh juice, and essence— / having prepared an errhine with these combined with long pepper and asafoetida, he does not sink down.

2.10.s:
niśā jyotiṣmatī pāṭhā kṛṣṇā kuṣṭhā vacā madhu ..
jihvāstambhe ca lepo'yaṃ guḍamūtrayuto hitaḥ .. 2.46.20 ..
2.10.d:
निशा ज्योतिष्मती पाठा कृष्णा कुष्ठा वचा मधु ॥
जिह्वास्तम्भे च लेपोऽयं गुडमूत्रयुतो हितः ॥ 2.46.20 ॥
2.10.m: Turmeric, jyotiṣmatī, pāṭhā, long pepper, kuṣṭha, vacā, and honey; / for stiffness of the tongue, this plaster mixed with jaggery and urine is beneficial.

2.10.s:
tilairyuktā rajanyā ca nimbapatraiśca yojitā ..
kṣaudreṇa śodhanī piṇḍī sarpiṣā vraṇaropiṇī .. 21 ..
2.10.d:
तिलैर्युक्ता रजन्या च निम्बपत्रैश्च योजिता ॥
क्षौद्रेण शोधनी पिण्डी सर्पिषा व्रणरोपिणी ॥ 21 ॥
2.10.m: Mixed with sesame and turmeric, and combined with neem leaves: / with honey, it is a cleansing bolus; with ghee, it heals wounds.

2.10.s:
abhighātena khañjanti yenāśvāstīvravedanāḥ ..
pariṣekakriyā teṣāṃ tailenāśu rujāpahā ..22..
2.10.d:
अभिघातेन खञ्जन्ति येनाश्वास्तीव्रवेदनाः ॥
परिषेकक्रिया तेषां तैलेनाशु रुजापहा ॥22॥
2.10.m: When horses limp due to an injury and suffer intense pain, / an affusion with oil quickly takes away their pain.

2.10.s:
doṣakopābhighātābhyāṃ tilaje jṛmbhate sadā ..
śāntirmadhvājyabandhābhyāṃ pakvambhinne vraṇe kramaḥ .. 23 ..
2.10.d:
दोषकोपाभिघाताभ्यां तिलजे जृम्भते सदा ॥
शान्तिर्मध्वाज्यबन्धाभ्यां पक्वम्भिन्ने व्रणे क्रमः ॥ 23 ॥
2.10.m: If it constantly gapes open from sesame-oil [application] due to vitiation of the humors or an injury, / relief comes through honey and ghee with bandaging; such is the method when the wound is ripe and burst.

2.10.s:
aśvatthodumbaraplakṣamadhūkavaṭakalkakaiḥ..
prabhūtasalilaḥ kvāthaḥ sukhoṣṇo vraṇaśodhanaḥ .. 24 ..
2.10.d:
अश्वत्थोदुम्बरप्लक्षमधूकवटकल्ककैः॥
प्रभूतसलिलः क्वाथः सुखोष्णो व्रणशोधनः ॥ 24 ॥
2.10.m: With pastes of aśvattha, udumbara, plakṣa, madhūka, and vaṭa, / a lukewarm decoction with plenty of water cleanses wounds.

2.10.s:
śatāhvā nāgaraṃ rāsnā mañjiṣṭhākuṣṭhasaindhavaiḥ ..
devadāruvacāyugmarajanīraktacandanaiḥ .. 25 ..
2.10.d:
शताह्वा नागरं रास्ना मञ्जिष्ठाकुष्ठसैन्धवैः ॥
देवदारुवचायुग्मरजनीरक्तचन्दनैः ॥ 25 ॥
2.10.m: With dill, ginger, rāsnā, madder, kuṣṭha, and rock salt, / deodar, vacā, the two turmerics, and red sandalwood,

2.10.s:
tailaṃ siddhaṃ kaṣāyeṇa guḍūcyā payasā saha ..
prakṣīṇe vastinasye ca yojyaṃ sarvatra laṃghane .. 26 ..
2.10.d:
तैलं सिद्धं कषायेण गुडूच्या पयसा सह ॥
प्रक्षीणे वस्तिनस्ये च योज्यं सर्वत्र लंघने ॥ 26 ॥
2.10.m: oil prepared with a decoction of guḍūcī together with milk / is to be used in wasting, as an enema, as an errhine, and universally in fasting therapy.

2.10.s:
raktasrāvo jalaukābhirnetrānte netrarogiṇaḥ ..
khadirodumbarāśvatthakaṣāyeṇa ca dhāvanam .. 27 ..
2.10.d:
रक्तस्रावो जलौकाभिर्नेत्रान्ते नेत्ररोगिणः ॥
खदिरोदुम्बराश्वत्थकषायेण च धावनम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.10.m: For a horse with eye disease, blood-letting by leeches is done at the outer corner of the eye, / and washing with a decoction of khadira, udumbara, and aśvattha.

2.10.s:
dhātrīdurālabhātiktā priyaṅgukuṅkumaiḥ samaiḥ ..
guḍūcyā kṛtakaḥ kalko hitamuṣṇāvalambite .. .. 28 ..
2.10.d:
धात्रीदुरालभातिक्ता प्रियङ्गुकुङ्कुमैः समैः ॥
गुडूच्या कृतकः कल्को हितमुष्णावलम्बिते ॥ ॥ 28 ॥
2.10.m: With equal parts of āmalakī, durālabhā, tiktā, priyaṅgu, and saffron, / a paste prepared with guḍūcī is beneficial when affected by heat.

2.10.s:
upānte ca śirāsrāve muṣkaśophe tathaiva ca ..
kṣiprakāriṇi doṣe ca sadyo vedhanamiṣyate .. 29 ..
2.10.d:
उपान्ते च शिरास्रावे मुष्कशोफे तथैव च ॥
क्षिप्रकारिणि दोषे च सद्यो वेधनमिष्यते ॥ 29 ॥
2.10.m: Near the border, vein-bleeding [is done], as well as in swelling of the scrotum; / and when the morbid humor acts swiftly, immediate vein-puncturing is desired.

2.10.s:
gośakṛtsarjikākuṣṭharajanītilasarṣapaiḥ ..
gavāṃ mūtreṇa piṣṭaiśca mardanaṃ kaṇḍunāśanam .. 2.46.30 ..
2.10.d:
गोशकृत्सर्जिकाकुष्ठरजनीतिलसर्षपैः ॥
गवां मूत्रेण पिष्टैश्च मर्दनं कण्डुनाशनम् ॥ 2.46.30 ॥
2.10.m: With cow dung, carbonate of soda, kuṣṭha, turmeric, sesame, and mustard, / ground with cow's urine, massage destroys itching.

2.10.s:
sitāmadhuyutaḥ kvātho vāśikāyāḥ saśarkaraḥ ..
raktapittaharaḥ pānādaśvakarṇāttathaiva ca .. 31 ..
2.10.d:
सितामधुयुतः क्वाथो वाशिकायाः सशर्करः ॥
रक्तपित्तहरः पानादश्वकर्णात्तथैव च ॥ 31 ॥
2.10.m: A decoction of vāsā with sugar candy and honey, sweetened with sugar, / cures bleeding disease through drinking, as does [a decoction] of aśvakarṇa.

2.10.s:
āme pariṇate pakvaṃ pakvamāṃse jarāṃ gate ..
pakvamāṃsayutaṃ neṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ jīrṇaṃ praśasyate .. 32 ..
2.10.d:
आमे परिणते पक्वं पक्वमांसे जरां गते ॥
पक्वमांसयुतं नेष्टं सर्वं जीर्णं प्रशस्यते ॥ 32 ॥
2.10.m: When raw, it is digested into cooked; when cooked meat has gone to digestion, / [food] combined with cooked meat is not desired; everything [fully] digested is praised.

2.10.s:
saptamesaptame deyamaśvānāṃ lavaṇaṃ dine ..
tathā bhuktavatāṃ deyā paripāne tu vāruṇī .. 33 ..
2.10.d:
सप्तमेसप्तमे देयमश्वानां लवणं दिने ॥
तथा भुक्तवतां देया परिपाने तु वारुणी ॥ 33 ॥
2.10.m: Salt is to be given to horses every seventh day; / likewise, to those who have eaten, vāruṇī liquor should be given as an after-drink.

2.10.s:
jīvanīyaiḥ sumadhurairmṛdvīkāśarkarāyutaiḥ ..
sapippalīkaiḥ śaradi pratimānaṃ sapadmakam .. 34 ..
2.10.d:
जीवनीयैः सुमधुरैर्मृद्वीकाशर्करायुतैः ॥
सपिप्पलीकैः शरदि प्रतिमानं सपद्मकम् ॥ 34 ॥
2.10.m: In autumn, an after-drink with life-giving drugs, very sweet, with raisins and sugar, / together with long pepper and padmaka [should be given].

2.10.s:
viḍaṅgapippalīdhānyāśatāhvā rodhrasaindhavaiḥ ..
sāvitrakaisturaṅgāṇāṃ pratipānaṃ himāgame .. 35 ...
2.10.d:
विडङ्गपिप्पलीधान्याशताह्वा रोध्रसैन्धवैः ॥
सावित्रकैस्तुरङ्गाणां प्रतिपानं हिमागमे ॥ 35 ॥।
2.10.m: With viḍaṅga, long pepper, coriander, dill, lodhra, and rock salt, / along with sun-plant seeds, [is] the after-drink for horses at the onset of cold.

2.10.s:
rodhraṃ priyaṅgukā rāsnā pippalīviśvabheṣajaiḥ ..
sakṣaudraiḥ pratipānaṃ syādvasante kaphanāśanam .. 36 ..
2.10.d:
रोध्रं प्रियङ्गुका रास्ना पिप्पलीविश्वभेषजैः ॥
सक्षौद्रैः प्रतिपानं स्याद्वसन्ते कफनाशनम् ॥ 36 ॥
2.10.m: With lodhra, priyaṅgu, rāsnā, long pepper, and dry ginger, / mixed with honey, there should be an after-drink in spring to destroy kapha.

2.10.s:
priyaṅgupippalīraudrayaṣṭyāhvaiḥ samahauṣadhaiḥ ..
nidāghe saguḍā deyā madirāpratipānake .. 37 ..
2.10.d:
प्रियङ्गुपिप्पलीरौद्रयष्ट्याह्वैः समहौषधैः ॥
निदाघे सगुडा देया मदिराप्रतिपानके ॥ 37 ॥
2.10.m: With priyaṅgu, long pepper, lodhra, liquorice, and ginger, / liquor mixed with jaggery should be given as an after-drink in summer.

2.10.s:
bhadrakāṣṭhā salavaṇaṃ pippalyā viśvabheṣajam ..
bhavettailayutairebhiḥ pratipānaṃ ghanāgame .. 38 ..
2.10.d:
भद्रकाष्ठा सलवणं पिप्पल्या विश्वभेषजम् ॥
भवेत्तैलयुतैरेभिः प्रतिपानं घनागमे ॥ 38 ॥
2.10.m: Deodar, together with salt, long pepper, and ginger— / combined with oil, these make an after-drink at the onset of the rains.

2.10.s:
nidāghāvṛtapittānāṃ kṣaranmadoṣṇaśoṇitāḥ ..
prāvṛḍbhinnapurīṣāśca pibeyurvājino ghṛtam .. 39 ..
2.10.d:
निदाघावृतपित्तानां क्षरन्मदोष्णशोणिताः ॥
प्रावृड्भिन्नपुरीषाश्च पिबेयुर्वाजिनो घृतम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.10.m: Horses whose pitta is aggravated in summer, exuding ichor and hot blood, / and whose stool is loose during the rainy season, should drink clarified butter.

2.10.s:
pibeyurvājinastailaṃ kaphavāyvadhikāstu ye ..
snehavyāpadbhavedyeṣāṃ teṣāṃ kāryaṃ virūkṣaṇam .. 2.46.40 ..
2.10.d:
पिबेयुर्वाजिनस्तैलं कफवाय्वधिकास्तु ये ॥
स्नेहव्यापद्भवेद्येषां तेषां कार्यं विरूक्षणम् ॥ 2.46.40 ॥
2.10.m: Horses that have an excess of kapha and vāta should drink oil; / for those who suffer complications from oleation, drying therapy must be performed.

2.10.s:
tryahaṃ yavāgū rūkṣā syātsurā ca lavaṇānvitā ..
bhojane takrasaṃyuktaṃ hyeṣa vai rūkṣaṇe vidhiḥ .. 41 ..
2.10.d:
त्र्यहं यवागू रूक्षा स्यात्सुरा च लवणान्विता ॥
भोजने तक्रसंयुक्तं ह्येष वै रूक्षणे विधिः ॥ 41 ॥
2.10.m: For three days there should be unctuousless gruel and wine mixed with salt, / and with meals [food] mixed with buttermilk; this indeed is the rule for drying therapy.

2.10.s:
prāyogikastathā deyo vastistasya niratyayaḥ ..
ye pibanti hayāḥ snehaṃ teṣāṃ vastiṃ na dāpayet .. 42 ..
2.10.d:
प्रायोगिकस्तथा देयो वस्तिस्तस्य निरत्ययः ॥
ये पिबन्ति हयाः स्नेहं तेषां वस्तिं न दापयेत् ॥ 42 ॥
2.10.m: Likewise, an enema suited to practice should be given to him without mishap; / one should not administer an enema to horses that are drinking unctuous substances.

2.10.s:
śarannidāghayoḥ sarpistailaṃ śītavasantayoḥ ..
varṣāsu śiśire caiva vastau deyamiheṣyate .. 43 ..
2.10.d:
शरन्निदाघयोः सर्पिस्तैलं शीतवसन्तयोः ॥
वर्षासु शिशिरे चैव वस्तौ देयमिहेष्यते ॥ 43 ॥
2.10.m: Ghee is desired here in autumn and summer, and oil in the cold season and spring; / in the rainy season and the winter season, [oil] should be given as an enema.

2.10.s:
gurvabhiṣyandibhaktāni vyāyāmaḥ snānamātapam ..
pāyurvastaṃ ca vāhasya snehapīḍasya varjitam.. 44 ..
2.10.d:
गुर्वभिष्यन्दिभक्तानि व्यायामः स्नानमातपम् ॥
पायुर्वस्तं च वाहस्य स्नेहपीडस्य वर्जितम्॥ 44 ॥
2.10.m: Heavy and channel-blocking meals, exercise, bathing, sunshine, / and checking the rectum are forbidden for a horse suffering from oleation.

2.10.s:
snānaṃ pānaṃ sakṛddṛṣṭamaśvānāṃ salilāgame ..
atyarthadurdine kāle snānamekaṃ praśasyate .. 45 ..
2.10.d:
स्नानं पानं सकृद्दृष्टमश्वानां सलिलागमे ॥
अत्यर्थदुर्दिने काले स्नानमेकं प्रशस्यते ॥ 45 ॥
2.10.m: Bathing and drinking once [a day] are seen for horses at the onset of the rains; / in very stormy weather, only bathing is commended.

2.10.s:
yuktaśītātape kāle dviḥ pānaṃ lavaṇaṃ sakṛt ..
grīṣme triḥ snānapānaṃ syācciraṃ tasyāvagāhanam .. 46 ..
2.10.d:
युक्तशीतातपे काले द्विः पानं लवणं सकृत् ॥
ग्रीष्मे त्रिः स्नानपानं स्याच्चिरं तस्यावगाहनम् ॥ 46 ॥
2.10.m: In a season of balanced cold and heat, drinking twice and salt once [are prescribed]; / in summer, bathing and drinking should be three times, and his immersion [should be] prolonged.

2.10.s:
nistuṣāṇāṃ pradātavyaṃ yavānāṃ caturāḍhakam ..
vavarṇavrīhimaudālākalanāṃ vāpi dāpayet .. 47 ..
2.10.d:
निस्तुषाणां प्रदातव्यं यवानां चतुराढकम् ॥
ववर्णव्रीहिमौदालाकलनां वापि दापयेत् ॥ 47 ॥
2.10.m: Four āḍhakas of husked barley should be given; / or one may give a measured portion of grain, rice, or bean-flour.

2.10.s:
ahorātreṇa cāndrasya yavasasya tulā daśa ..
aṣṭau śuṣkasya dātavyāścatasro'tha busasya vā .. 48 ..
2.10.d:
अहोरात्रेण चान्द्रस्य यवसस्य तुला दश ॥
अष्टौ शुष्कस्य दातव्याश्चतस्रोऽथ बुसस्य वा ॥ 48 ॥
2.10.m: In a day and night, ten tulās of moist fodder / or eight [tulās] of dry [fodder] should be given, or four of chaff.

2.10.s:
dūrvā pittaṃ busaḥ kārśyaṃ tadbusaḥ śleṣmasañcayam ..
nāśayatyarjunaḥ śvāsaṃ tathā māṣo balakṣayam .. 49 ..
2.10.d:
दूर्वा पित्तं बुसः कार्श्यं तद्बुसः श्लेष्मसञ्चयम् ॥
नाशयत्यर्जुनः श्वासं तथा माषो बलक्षयम् ॥ 49 ॥
2.10.m: Dūrvā destroys bile, chaff [destroys] emaciation, and that chaff [destroys] accumulation of phlegm; / arjuna destroys dyspnoea, and likewise black gram [destroys] loss of strength.

2.10.s:
vātikāḥ paittikāścaiva śleṣmajāḥ sānnipātikāḥ ..
na rogāḥ pīḍayiṣyanti dūrvāhāraṃ turaṅgamam .. 2.46.50..
2.10.d:
वातिकाः पैत्तिकाश्चैव श्लेष्मजाः सान्निपातिकाः ॥
न रोगाः पीडयिष्यन्ति दूर्वाहारं तुरङ्गमम् ॥ 2.46.50॥
2.10.m: Diseases arising from wind, from bile, from phlegm, or from their combination / will not afflict a horse that feeds on dūrvā.

2.10.s:
dvau rajjubandhau duṣṭānāṃ pakṣayorubhayorapi ..
paścādbandhaśca kartavyo harakīlavyapāśrayaḥ .. 51 ..
2.10.d:
द्वौ रज्जुबन्धौ दुष्टानां पक्षयोरुभयोरपि ॥
पश्चाद्बन्धश्च कर्तव्यो हरकीलव्यपाश्रयः ॥ 51 ॥
2.10.m: For vicious [horses], two rope-bindings should be made on both flanks, / and a rear binding attached to a post should be constructed.

2.10.s:
keśānurūpamāsyasya keśapucchaprakalpanam ..
chedaḥ khurapravṛddhau ca varjayettu kanīnikām .. 52 ..
2.10.d:
केशानुरूपमास्यस्य केशपुच्छप्रकल्पनम् ॥
छेदः खुरप्रवृद्धौ च वर्जयेत्तु कनीनिकाम् ॥ 52 ॥
2.10.m: Trimming of the hair and tail should be done to match the hair of the face; / and when the hooves overgrow, trimming [is done], but one must avoid the inner corner [of the hoof].

2.10.s:
yatnopanyastayavasaḥ kṛtadhūpanabhūmayaḥ ..
vaseyuḥ sambhṛte sthāne pradīpaiḥ sārvarātrikaiḥ .. 53 ..
2.10.d:
यत्नोपन्यस्तयवसः कृतधूपनभूमयः ॥
वसेयुः सम्भृते स्थाने प्रदीपैः सार्वरात्रिकैः ॥ 53 ॥
2.10.m: With grass carefully laid down and the ground fumigated, / they should dwell in a well-equipped stall with lamps [kept burning] through the whole night.

2.10.s:
śākhāmṛgojāḥ kṛkavākavaśca dhāryāśca śālāsu tathaiva dhenuḥ ..
kuryurniśīthe puruṣāḥ saśastrāḥ saṃrakṣaṇaṃ rāma turaṅgamāṇām .. 54 .. ..
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare dvitīyakhaṇḍe mā0 saṃ0 rāmaṃ prati puṣkaropākhyāne aśvacikitsā nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 46 .. .. cha ..
2.47
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ śāntikarma nibodha me ..
pañcamīṣu ca sarvāsu śrīdharaṃ pūjayedbhṛśam ..1..
śriyaśca pūjanaṃ kāryaṃ hayarājñastathaiva va ..
rāmoccaiḥśravaso nityaṃ gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ .. .. 2 ..
dhūpadīpanamaskāraistathā caivānnasampadā ..
śaradvasantayoḥ kāryamekadantasya pūjanam .. 3 ..
pratipatpañcamī ṣaṣṭhī saptamī dvādaśī tathā ..
praśastāstithayo rāma sūryavāro viśeṣataḥ .. 4 ..
2.10.d:
शाखामृगोजाः कृकवाकवश्च धार्याश्च शालासु तथैव धेनुः ॥
कुर्युर्निशीथे पुरुषाः सशस्त्राः संरक्षणं राम तुरङ्गमाणाम् ॥ 54 ॥ ॥
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मा0 सं0 रामं प्रति पुष्करोपाख्याने अश्वचिकित्सा नाम षट्चत्वारिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः ॥ 46 ॥ ॥ छ ॥
2.47
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं शान्तिकर्म निबोध मे ॥
पञ्चमीषु च सर्वासु श्रीधरं पूजयेद्भृशम् ॥1॥
श्रियश्च पूजनं कार्यं हयराज्ञस्तथैव व ॥
रामोच्चैःश्रवसो नित्यं गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
धूपदीपनमस्कारैस्तथा चैवान्नसम्पदा ॥
शरद्वसन्तयोः कार्यमेकदन्तस्य पूजनम् ॥ 3 ॥
प्रतिपत्पञ्चमी षष्ठी सप्तमी द्वादशी तथा ॥
प्रशस्तास्तिथयो राम सूर्यवारो विशेषतः ॥ 4 ॥
2.10.m:
Monkeys, goats, and roosters should be kept in the stables, and likewise a milk-cow; / armed men should keep guard over the horses at midnight, O Rāma.
Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, named 'Treatment of Horses', in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma in the conversation of Mārkaṇḍeya, in the second book of the auspicious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Puṣkara said: / Learn from me the regular, occasional, and optional rite of pacification. / On every fifth lunar day one should fervently worship the bearer of Śrī;
and worship should be paid to Śrī and likewise to the king of horses, / O Rāma, to Uccaiḥśravas, constantly with perfumes, garlands, and unguents,
with incenses, lamps, salutations, and an abundance of food. / In autumn and spring, worship of Ekadanta should be performed.
The first, fifth, sixth, seventh, and twelfth lunar days / are praised, O Rāma, especially Sunday.

2.10.s:
kṛttikāṃ rohiṇīṃ bhāgyaṃ cāryamṇamaśvinīṃ tathā ..
tvāṣṭraṃ sāvitramādityaṃ vāyavyaṃ ca bhṛgūttama .. .. 5 ..
nakṣatrāṇi praśastāni śuklapakṣastathaiva ca ..
udyāneṣu vicitreṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca .. 6 ..
devatāyatanaṃ rāma pūjanaṃ tasya kārayet ..
arghadhūpanamaskāradīpapuṣpānnasampadā .. 7 ..
kulmāṣollopikābhakṣyamadyamāṃsasurāsavaiḥ ..
odanaiḥ paramānnena phalaiḥ kālodbhavaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 8 ..
nṛtya gītena vādyena śaṅkhaśabdaistathaiva ca ..
sāvitraiśca tathaivājyaṃ juhuyājjātavedasi .. 9 ..
oṃkārapūrvaṃ ca tathā revantāya punaḥpunaḥ ..
dvijātipūjanaṃ kāryaṃ mālyamodakacandanaiḥ .. 2.47.10 ..
dakṣiṇābhiśca dharmajña yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ ..
nārīṣu varjayetsarvaṃ revantasya niveditam .. 11 ..
evaṃ sampūjito dadyātturaṅgamaśatānyapi ..
balaṃ tejastathārogyaṃ turaṅgāṇāṃ ca bhārgava .. 12..
2.10.d:
कृत्तिकां रोहिणीं भाग्यं चार्यम्णमश्विनीं तथा ॥
त्वाष्ट्रं सावित्रमादित्यं वायव्यं च भृगूत्तम ॥ ॥ 5 ॥
नक्षत्राणि प्रशस्तानि शुक्लपक्षस्तथैव च ॥
उद्यानेषु विचित्रेषु नदीनां पुलिनेषु च ॥ 6 ॥
देवतायतनं राम पूजनं तस्य कारयेत् ॥
अर्घधूपनमस्कारदीपपुष्पान्नसम्पदा ॥ 7 ॥
कुल्माषोल्लोपिकाभक्ष्यमद्यमांससुरासवैः ॥
ओदनैः परमान्नेन फलैः कालोद्भवैः शुभैः ॥ 8 ॥
नृत्य गीतेन वाद्येन शङ्खशब्दैस्तथैव च ॥
सावित्रैश्च तथैवाज्यं जुहुयाज्जातवेदसि ॥ 9 ॥
ओंकारपूर्वं च तथा रेवन्ताय पुनःपुनः ॥
द्विजातिपूजनं कार्यं माल्यमोदकचन्दनैः ॥ 2.47.10 ॥
दक्षिणाभिश्च धर्मज्ञ यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥
नारीषु वर्जयेत्सर्वं रेवन्तस्य निवेदितम् ॥ 11 ॥
एवं सम्पूजितो दद्यात्तुरङ्गमशतान्यपि ॥
बलं तेजस्तथारोग्यं तुरङ्गाणां च भार्गव ॥ 12॥
2.10.m:
Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Bhāgya, Āryamṇa, and Aśvinī, / Tvāṣṭra, Sāvitra, Āditya, and Vāyavya, O foremost of the Bhṛgus—
these asterisms are praised, as is the bright fortnight. / In picturesque gardens and on sandy riverbanks,
or in a shrine of the gods, O Rāma, one should perform his worship / with water of hospitality, incense, salutations, lamps, flowers, and an abundance of food;
with boiled half-ripe grains, stuffed sweetmeats, food-preparations, liquor, meat, spirituous drinks, and wines; / with boiled rice, payasa, and auspicious fruits produced in season;
with dance, song, instrumental music, and the sounds of conches. / And one should offer ghee into the fire with the verses addressed to Savitṛ,
preceded by the syllable Om, again and again to Revanta. / Worship of the twice-born should be performed with garlands, sweetmeats, and sandalwood,
and with sacrificial fees in proper order, O knower of dharma. / One should withhold from women everything offered to Revanta.
Worshipped thus, he grants hundreds of horses, / and strength, fiery energy, and health to horses, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.10.s:
aśvayukśuklapakṣasya pañcadaśyāṃ narottama ..
turaṅgamāṇāṃ kartavyaṃ śāntikaṃ tannibodha me..13..
digīśānīṃ viniṣkṛṣya grāmāddeśe manorame..
prāgudakpravaṇe rāma sthaṇḍilaṃ parikalpayet ..14..
nāsatyau varuṇaṃ devaṃ tathaivāśvayuje dvija ..
pūjayetprayato vidvāngandhamālyānulepanaiḥ..15..
dhūpairdīpairnamaskāraistathā cānnena bhūriṇā ..
samullikhya tato vediṃ śākhābhiḥ parivārayet ..16..
samantatastathārdrābhirvastraiścāpyahataistathā ..
ghaṭānsarvarasaiḥ pūrṇāndikṣu dadyādyathāvidhi ..17..
vidikṣu ca tathā dadyāddhvajacchatrāṇi buddhimān ..
tataḥ samupadhāyāgniṃ jayaprabhṛtibhiḥ punaḥ .. 18..
hutvoktadevatāliṅgairmantraiśca juhuyādghṛtam ..
tataḥ sampūjanīyāstu gandhamālyaisturaṅgamā ..19..
2.10.d:
अश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्यां नरोत्तम ॥
तुरङ्गमाणां कर्तव्यं शान्तिकं तन्निबोध मे॥13॥
दिगीशानीं विनिष्कृष्य ग्रामाद्देशे मनोरमे॥
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे राम स्थण्डिलं परिकल्पयेत् ॥14॥
नासत्यौ वरुणं देवं तथैवाश्वयुजे द्विज ॥
पूजयेत्प्रयतो विद्वान्गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः॥15॥
धूपैर्दीपैर्नमस्कारैस्तथा चान्नेन भूरिणा ॥
समुल्लिख्य ततो वेदिं शाखाभिः परिवारयेत् ॥16॥
समन्ततस्तथार्द्राभिर्वस्त्रैश्चाप्यहतैस्तथा ॥
घटान्सर्वरसैः पूर्णान्दिक्षु दद्याद्यथाविधि ॥17॥
विदिक्षु च तथा दद्याद्ध्वजच्छत्राणि बुद्धिमान् ॥
ततः समुपधायाग्निं जयप्रभृतिभिः पुनः ॥ 18॥
हुत्वोक्तदेवतालिङ्गैर्मन्त्रैश्च जुहुयाद्घृतम् ॥
ततः सम्पूजनीयास्तु गन्धमाल्यैस्तुरङ्गमा ॥19॥
2.10.m:
On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month Aśvayuj, O best of men, / the pacification rite for horses should be performed; learn it from me.
Having gone out from the village toward the north-east to a pleasant place, / sloping to the east or north, O Rāma, one should prepare an altar-mound.
To the two Nāsatyas, to the god Varuṇa, and to Aśvayuj, O twice-born, / the wise man, composed, should offer worship with perfumes, garlands, and unguents,
with incenses, lamps, salutations, and abundant food. / Then, having outlined the altar, he should enclose it with branches,
and on all sides with fresh, unwashed garments. / In the cardinal directions he should place pots filled with all fluids according to rule;
and in the intermediate directions the wise man should set up banners and parasols. / Then, having established the fire, again with the Jaya mantras and others,
and having made oblations with the mantras that indicate the specified deities, he should offer clarified butter. / Then the horses are to be worshipped with perfumes and garlands.

2.10.d:
सन्नद्धपुरुषारूढाः सुसन्नद्धास्तुरङ्गमाः ॥
सायुधैः पुरुषैः सार्धं वह्निं कुर्युः प्रदक्षिणम् ॥2.47.20॥
त्रिः परिक्रामतो वह्निं क्ष्वेडोत्कृष्टनिनादितैः ॥
शङ्खवाद्यरवोन्मिश्रैर्नेतव्याः स्वगृहं ततः ॥ 21 ॥
रसानि तानि वासांसि गौः कांस्यं कनकं तथा ॥
दक्षिणायै प्रदातव्यं कर्तुर्द्विजवरोत्तम ॥ 22 ॥
कर्मणानेन भवति प्रभूतं राम वाहनम् ॥
हृष्टपुष्टं च धर्मज्ञ गदामयविवर्जितम् ॥ 23 ॥
नित्यमेतत्तवोद्दिष्टं शृणु नैमित्तिकं तथा ॥
अश्वानां मारके प्राप्ते व्याधौ वाप्यतिदारुणे ॥ 24 ॥
प्रकृतेश्च विपर्यासे तथा भृगुकुलोद्भव ॥
हयचारे शुभे देशे स्थण्डिलं परिकल्पयेत् ॥ 25 ॥
विन्यसेत्कमलं तत्र तन्मध्ये पूजयेद्धरिम् ॥
श्रियं च देवीं तत्रैव केसरेषु च देवताः ॥ 26 ॥
2.10.m:
Mounted by fully-armored men, the well-armored horses, / accompanied by armed men, should circumambulate the fire.
Having circumambulated the fire three times amidst roarings and cries of triumph, / mingled with the sounds of conches and instruments, they should then be led to their stall.
Those fluids, garments, a cow, bell-metal, and gold / should be given as a sacrificial fee to the officiating priest, O best of twice-born.
Through this rite, one's mounts become plentiful, O Rāma, / vigorous, sturdy, and free from sickness and disease, O knower of dharma.
This regular rite has been described to you; now hear the occasional one: / when a pestilence strikes horses, or when a very terrible disease occurs,
or when an unnatural alteration happens, O descendant of Bhṛgu's lineage, / one should prepare an altar-mound in a pure place in the horse enclosure.
One should draw a lotus there; in its center one should worship Hari / and the goddess Śrī right there, and in the filaments the deities:

ब्रह्माणं शङ्करं सोममादित्यं च तथाश्विनौ ॥
रेवन्तमुच्चैःश्रवसं दिक्पालाम्̐श्च दलेष्वपि ॥ 27 ॥
सर्वेषां पूजनं कार्यं गन्धधूपान्नसम्पदा ॥
दीपमाल्यनमस्कारपुष्पैर्मूलैः सगोरसैः॥28॥
प्रत्येकं पूर्णकुम्भैश्च गन्धमाल्याद्यलङ्कृतैः ॥
तथा पिशितवस्त्रैश्च वर्धमानैः सतण्डुलैः ॥ 29 ॥
तथा प्रतिसरासूत्रैः पताकाभिश्च भार्गव ॥
तस्यै वोत्तरतो वेदिं कल्पयित्वा यथाविधि ॥ 2.47.30 ॥
ततः समुपधायाग्निं यथोक्तानां पृथक्पृथक् ॥
ततोऽग्निहवनस्यानु कांस्यं गां काञ्चनं तथा ॥ 31 ॥
देयं वस्त्रयुगं कर्त्रे कारयित्रे तथैव च ॥
कर्मैतत्सर्वरोगघ्नं सर्वबाधाविनाशनम् ॥ 32 ॥
उपोषितेन कर्तव्यं ब्राह्मणेन यथाविधि ॥
उपोषितस्तदा तिष्ठेद्यजमानोऽपि भार्गव ॥ 33 ॥
2.10.m:
Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Soma, Āditya, and the two Aśvins, / Revanta, Uccaiḥśravas, and the guardians of the directions upon the petals.
Worship of all of them should be performed with perfume, incense, an abundance of food, / lamps, garlands, salutations, flowers, roots, and milk-products;
for each [deity] with full jars adorned with perfumes, garlands, and the like, / with dishes of meat, vessels filled with rice grains,
and with protective amulets and banners, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Having prepared an altar to the north of it according to rule,
and having then established the fire, [offering] to each of the deities mentioned, / then, following the oblation into the fire, bell-metal, a cow, and gold,
and a pair of garments must be given to the officiant and likewise to the patron. / This rite destroys all diseases and dispels all afflictions.
It should be performed according to rule by a fasting brahmin; / the patron too should remain fasting at that time, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.10.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि काम्यं कर्म तवानघ ॥
उपोषितौ सदा पौष्णे यजमानपुरोहितौ ॥34॥
अश्विनर्क्षे सदा स्नानं कुर्युर्यन्मे निबोधत ॥
अकालमूलौ द्वौ कुम्भौ मधूककुसुमोत्कटौ ॥ 35 ॥
अश्वगन्धायुतौ कृत्वा स्नाप्यस्ताभ्यां तदा भवेत् ॥
उत्तमं पूजयेद्विद्वान्नासत्यौ शशिनं तथा ॥ 36 ॥
अश्विनौ वरुणं चैव शुक्लवासास्तथा हरिम् ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥ 37 ॥
ततोऽश्वमिथुनं कार्यं सर्वौषधियुतं मृदा ॥
प्रणतेन ततो विद्वान्नासत्याभ्यां निवेदयेत् ॥ 38 ॥
धूपमश्वशफं दद्याद्दैवतानां तथैव च ॥
यथोक्तानां द्विजश्रेष्ठ जुहुयाच्च पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 39 ॥
चतुर्थ्यन्तेन नाम्ना तु प्रणवाद्येन भार्गव ॥
स्वाहान्तेनाथ शतशो मन्त्रपूतं घृतं द्विज ॥ 2.47.40 ॥
2.10.m:
Hereafter I shall declare to you the optional rite, O sinless one. / The patron and the priest should always fast on [the asterism] Pauṣṇa;
they should always perform a bath under the asterism Aśvinī, which learn from me: / two water-jars containing untimely roots, filled with Madhūka blossoms,
and combined with aśvagandhā, being prepared, he should then be bathed with them. / The wise man should worship the highest [Lord], the two Nāsatyas, and the Moon.
Wearing white garments, [he should worship] the Aśvins, Varuṇa, and Hari, / with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food.
Then a pair of horses should be made of clay mixed with all medicinal herbs; / then, bowing down, the wise man should offer it to the two Nāsatyas.
He should offer horse-hoof as incense, and in the same way to the deities / as described, O best of the twice-born, he should offer oblations separately,
with their names in the dative case, preceded by the praṇava, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / and ending with 'svāhā', hundreds of times, with ghee purified by mantras, O twice-born.

अश्वलोम तथा धार्यं फलमूले तथैव च ॥
एकत्र त्रिवृतं कृत्वा मणिर्धार्यस्तु पूर्ववत् ॥ 41 ॥
अलंघयन्नश्विनतिं सदैव स्नानं च कुर्यात्प्रयता मनुष्यः ॥

2.48
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
कुञ्जराः परमा शोभा शिबिरस्य बलस्य च॥
आयाति कुञ्जरेष्वेव विजयः पृथिवीक्षिताम् ॥ 1 ॥
तेषां संमार्जने यत्नं पालने च भृगूत्तम ॥
यथावन्नृपतिः कुर्याद्गन्धर्वाः कुञ्जरा मताः ॥2॥
जयन्ताश्च तथा धार्या यावतां पोषणं सुखम् ॥
कर्तुं शक्यं न धार्यास्ते क्षुधिता दुःखितास्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
दुःखितास्ते नृणां हन्युः कुलानि च भृगूत्तम ॥
तस्मात्तेषां सुखं कार्यं यशःश्रीविजयप्रदम् ॥ 4 ॥
सन्नद्धपुरुषारूढैः सुसन्नद्धैस्तुरङ्गमैः ॥
अनल्पैरपि यद्युक्तं बलं परबलप्रणुत् ॥ 5॥।
2.10.m:
Horse hair should be worn, as well as fruits and roots; / having braided them together into three strands, an amulet should be worn as before.
Never omitting reverence to the Aśvins, a restrained man should always bathe; / he obtains horses by the thousands, born of noble breed, endowed with vigor and strength.
Puṣkara said: / Elephants are the supreme splendor of an encampment and of an army; / victory for earthly kings resides in elephants alone.
The king should duly take care in cleaning them and guarding them, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / elephants are regarded as gandharvas.
Only so many victorious [elephants] should be kept as can be comfortably nourished; / they should not be kept hungry and distressed.
When distressed, they would destroy the dynasties of men, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / therefore comfort should be given to them, which bestows fame, prosperity, and victory.
Even if an army capable of driving off the enemy's force is equipped / with numerous well-accoutred horses mounted by armoured warriors,

2.10.d:
तदैकस्यापि समरे कुञ्जरस्य सवर्मणः ॥
न शक्यं प्रमुखे स्थातुं वेगादापततो द्विज ॥6॥
अभिन्नानां तु संघानां संहृतानां च भेदनम् ॥
एकः क्रुद्धो रणे कुर्यात्कुञ्जरः साधु चोदितः ॥7॥
मदक्लिन्नकपोलस्य किञ्चिदञ्चितचक्षुषः ॥
बृहदाभोगशुण्डस्य कः शोभां कथितुं क्षमः ॥8॥
वेगेन धावमानस्य प्रसारितकरस्य च ॥
कः समर्थः पुरः स्थातुं स्तब्धकर्णस्य दन्तिनः ॥9॥
यस्य फूत्कारमात्रेण तुरङ्गमशतान्यपि॥
स्वारूढान्यपि वेगेन विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश॥2.48.10॥
तत्सैन्यं कुञ्जरा यत्र स नृपो यस्य कुञ्जराः ।
मूर्तिमान्विजयो राम कुञ्जरा मदगर्विताः ॥ 11 ॥
सपक्षा देववाह्यास्ते मनुजानां त्वपक्षकाः ॥
वाहनार्थं कृता राम स्वयमेव तु वेधसा ॥12॥
2.10.m:
even then, O twice-born, it is impossible to stand in battle in front / of even a single armoured elephant rushing with momentum.
A single enraged elephant, properly driven in battle, / can break unbroken arrays and consolidated troops.
Who is able to describe the splendor of one whose temples are wet with rut, / whose eyes are slightly curved, and whose trunk has a vast expanse?
Who is capable of standing before a tusker charging with speed, / with outstretched trunk and stiffened ears?
At whose mere snorting even hundreds of horses, / even well-mounted, swiftly scatter in the ten directions!
That is an army where elephants are; he is a king who possesses elephants; / elephants proud with rut, O Rāma, are victory incarnate.
Endowed with wings, they were the mounts of the gods; but for mortals, they were made wingless / for the purpose of riding, O Rāma, by the Creator himself.

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि कुञ्जराणां चिकित्सितम् ॥
पाकलेषु तु सर्वेषु कर्तव्यमनुवासरम् ॥ 1 ॥
घृततैलपरीषेकः स्थानं वातविवर्जितम् ॥
स्कन्धेषु च तथा कार्या क्रिया पाकलवद्द्विज ॥2॥
गोमूत्रं पाण्डुरोगे तु रजनीभिर्युतं हितम् ॥
आनाहे तैलसिक्तस्य निवातस्थं प्रशस्यते ॥3॥
लवणैः पञ्चभिर्मिश्रा प्रतिपानाय वारुणी ॥
विडङ्गत्रिफलाव्योषसैन्धवैः कवलाः कृताः ॥4॥
मूर्च्छास्वभोजयेन्नागं क्षौद्रतोयं तु पाययेत् ॥
अभ्यङ्गः शिरसः कार्यो नस्यश्चैव प्रशस्यते ॥ 5 ॥
नागानां स्नेहकटुकैः पादरोगानुपक्रमेत् ॥
पञ्चकल्ककषायेण शोधनं च विधीयते ॥ 6 ॥
2.10.m:
Seeing an army of noble elephants, mighty like a mountain and adorned with banners, / the hearts of enemies sink swiftly; therefore lordly elephants are always foremost.
Puṣkara said: / Hereafter I shall explain the medical treatment of elephants. / In all feverish conditions, [this] must be performed every day:
Sprinkling with ghee and oil, and a location free from wind; / and on the shoulders, O twice-born, treatment should be applied just as in fever.
In jaundice, cow's urine mixed with turmeric is beneficial; / in flatulence, staying in a place sheltered from wind is praised for one sprinkled with oil.
Vāruṇī wine mixed with the five salts should be given as a drink; / boluses should be prepared with viḍaṅga, triphalā, vyoṣa, and rock salt.
During fainting spells, one should not feed the elephant, but make him drink honey-water; / anointment of the head should be done, and errhine therapy is praised.
One should treat foot diseases of elephants with oily and pungent substances; / and cleansing is prescribed with a decoction of the five pastes.

2.10.m:
[…] rubbing should be done, and one should feed soft and unctuous food; / with the meat juices of peacocks, partridges, and quails, mixed with long pepper and black pepper,
one should feed the elephant when tremors arise in him. / Tender bilva fruit, lodhra, and dhātakī along with husked grain,
the elephant should eat as a bolus for the destruction of diarrhea. / In stiffness of the trunk, ghee mixed with salt should be given as an errhine.
Gruel prepared with buttermilk, rich in long pepper and black pepper [should be given], / and wild-boar broth should be placed in his ear.
Oil cooked with daśamūla, horsegram, sour gruel, and kākamācī, / mixed with black pepper, cures the disease of throat spasm.
He should make him drink clear liquor combined with the eight ground salts; / or in retention of urine, a boiled decoction of cucumber seeds.
In skin diseases, the elephant should drink neem or vāsā decoction; / cow's urine and viḍaṅga are recommended in worm infections.
Milk boiled with ginger, long pepper, grapes, and sugar / removes wounds and wasting when drunk, and wholesome meat-broth likewise.

2.10.m:
Rice cooked with mung beans and mixed with vyoṣa is commended in loss of appetite; / for soothing swelling of the throat, a soup of paṭolī, neem, and durgrāhyā [is recommended].
Trivṛt, vyoṣa, citraka, dantī, arka, śyāmā, spurge, and gajapippalī: / this medicated oil, and likewise an asava made of them, cures abdominal swellings.
Auspicious barks of milky trees, stream-jambū, and boswellia / should be given to alleviate heart disease, along with vidārī and boiled rice with broth.
By incision, blood-letting, unction, drinking of fats, and oily enemas, / he should treat all abscesses that have arisen.
He should drink sixty-day rice with mung-bean soup in autumn ailments; / and a plaster of tender bilva fruits is recommended in waist diseases.
Viḍaṅga, indrayava, asafoetida, pine resin, and the two turmerics: / he should give this bolus in the morning for the relief of all colic.
A tusker's tooth loosened by heavy load should be extracted. / Sixty-day rice, wild rice, and śāli rice are primary for their diet;
barley and wheat are middling, and the rest are remembered as inferior. / In preparing their food, one should carefully avoid burnt grain.

2.10.m:
Among fodders, sugarcane increases the strength of elephants; / dry fodder aggravates phlegm and wind in elephants.
Drinking milk is recommended for an elephant exhausted by mada; / likewise, meat broth cooked with vitalising substances is beneficial.
Hereafter, I shall declare recipes that promote mada, / which a king should employ when the time of battle has arrived.
Vāyasa, both kinds of kurava, kākolī, nākulī, and hari, / combined with honey, become a bolus that immediately induces rut.
A shoot of jātī along with its root, the bark of kapota, likewise iṅgudī, / and a shoot of aśvasāraka: this is another such bolus.
With ajaśṛṅgī and arka root, combined with kuñja and honey, / this bolus, mixed with honey and accompanied by flowers, roots, and fruits,
should be administered to the elephant in time of battle to increase mada. / Kaṭumatsyā, viḍaṅga, alkali, kośātakī, milk,

His bed should be made of dried dung and dust. / There should be sprinkling with oil in cold weather, month after month;
and in autumn and summer, sprinkling with ghee is prescribed. / A king should never make the decoration of another elephant greater than that of the state elephant; / indeed, a king should always arrange greater decoration for the state elephant alone.
Puṣkara said: / Hereafter, learn from me the pacification rites for elephants, / daily, occasional, and for specific desires, properly and in due order.
On the bright fifth lunar days, the worship of Vāsudeva, / of Śrī, O Rāma, and of the elephant Airāvaṇa should be performed,
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food; / and likewise at the end of the dark fortnight, month after month, O foremost of the twice-born,

at the confluences of rivers, in mountain caves, / at prominent junctions of three roads, and in deserted temples.

2.10.m:
Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are of divine origin. / One should carefully perform the worship of each of those mentioned, separately,
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food. / Likewise, there should be an oblation into fire with clarified butter purified by the syllable Oṃ,
separately for all of them with their names ending in the dative case. / Then, O Rāma, one should cause the brahmins to recite auspicious blessings with sacrificial fees.
Then, having prepared water for pacification, one should sprinkle the elephants / with the tip of kuśa grass using demon-slaying mantras; and they should then be honoured in the same manner.
Hereafter, I shall declare to you the occasional rite / upon the death of elephants or when a dreadful disease occurs,
upon the occurrence of inauspiciousness in cutting the tusks, or when the royal elephant dies, / or when a breaking of the tusk occurs, or when an elephant dies in the bright fortnight,
when an elephant dies in the dark fortnight, or when it dies on the "back of fire", / or at terrible moments, or with its head to the south-west,

or when rut occurs in a cow-elephant, or upon an unnatural change of behaviour. / In the north-eastern direction from the city, in a very charming [spot],
where the waters are pleasant to drink, filled with trees and forest monarchs, / one should prepare a ritual ground sloping to the north-east, O Rāma.
There one should draw a lotus; in the lotus pericarp, [one should place] Hari, / and there one should place Śrī; and on the filaments one should place
Brahmā, Bhārgava, Earth, and Skanda, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / Ananta, Space, Śiva, and Soma—all of these, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
On the petals there, one should place the guardians of the directions together with their elephants, / and between the petals the weapons, duly and in proper sequence.
The wise one should place the thunderbolt immediately after the petal of Śakra, / then the discus, then the staff, immediately after that the archway,
and then one should place the noose, the lance, the bow with an arrow, / then the club, O fortunate one, and then one should place the trident.

2.10.d:
पद्मञ्च सान्तरदलं वृत्तया लेखया भजेत् ॥
आदित्यैः सह नासत्यौ ततः पूर्वेण विन्यसेत् ॥ 25 ॥
वसूनग्निदिशाभागे साध्यान्याम्ये च विन्यसेत ॥
तथा च नैरृते भागे देवानङ्गिरसो न्यसेत् ॥ 26 ॥
पश्चिमे भृगवो भागे वायव्ये मरुतस्तथा ॥
विश्वेदेवास्तथोदक् च रुद्राञ्शिवदिशि न्यसेत् ॥ 27 ॥
कृत्वैतद्देवतान्यासं वृत्तया रेखया भजेत् ॥
बाह्येन विन्यसेत्तस्याः सूत्रकारानॄषीन्द्विज ॥ 28 ॥
पूर्वेण राम याम्येन तथा देवीं सरस्वतीम् ॥
नदीः पश्चिमतः शैलांस्तथोदग्भृगुनन्दन॥29॥
महाभूतानि वेदीषु कोणहस्तगतानि तु॥
पद्मं चक्रं गदां शङ्खमीशान्यादिषु विन्यसेत्॥ ॥। 2.50.30 ॥
चतुरस्रं तथा कार्यं चतुर्द्वारं च मण्डलम् ॥
प्रमाणं मण्डलस्यात्र भवेद्भूमिवशात्तथा ॥
विदिक्षु पूर्णकलशान्पूर्णपात्रयुतान्न्यसेत ॥ 31 ॥।
2.10.m:
And one should surround the lotus together with its intermediate petals with a circular line. / Then one should place the Nāsatyas along with the Ādityas in the east.
One should place the Vasus in the fire-quarter (southeast) and the Sādhyas in the southern quarter; / and in the southwest quarter one should place the divine Āṅgirasas.
In the western quarter, the Bhṛgus; and in the northwest, the Maruts; / likewise the Viśvedevas in the north, and one should place the Rudras in Śiva's quarter (northeast).
Having made this ritual placement of deities, one should divide [the space] with a circular line; / outside of it, twice-born one, one should place the sages who are authors of the sūtras.
In the east, O Rāma; in the south, the goddess Sarasvatī; / rivers in the west, and mountains in the north, O joy of the Bhṛgus.
The great elements on the altars located at the corner cubits; / one should place the lotus, discuss, club, and conch beginning with the northeast.
And a square sacred diagram should be made, having four doors; / the measure of the sacred diagram here should depend on the ground; / in the intermediate quarters one should place full jars accompanied by full bowls.

2.10.d:
सप्तहस्तेषु दण्डेषु पताकाश्च तथा न्यसेत् ॥
सिता रक्ताः सिताः पीता यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥
दिक्षु तोरणविन्यासं तोरणानां च वेष्टनम् ॥ 32 ॥
क्षीरवृक्षद्रुमदलैः कुसुमैः सफलैर्भवेत् ॥
तोरणस्य प्रमाणं च षड्ढस्तं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 33 ॥
उच्छ्रायेण तथा यामाज्ज्ञेयं राम समद्वयम् ॥
तार्क्ष्यं तालं च मकरं ऋष्यं चैवानुपूर्वशः ॥ 34 ॥
तोरणोपरि मध्ये तु दानवान्विनिवेशयेत् ॥
कर्णकैर्लक्षणोपेतान्विन्यसेद्देवतागणान् ॥ 35 ॥
सायुधान्सपताकाम्̐श्च सातपत्रं शतक्रतुम् ॥
दिग्गजानां च विन्यासमोषधीभिः प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 36 ॥
ऐरावणं दले शक्रे लाजाभिर्विन्यसेद्बुधः ॥
नागं पुष्पमयं पद्ममाग्नेये विन्यसेद्दले ॥ 37 ॥
पुष्पदन्तस्तथा याम्ये नागः कार्यः प्रियंगुभिः ॥
तथा च नैरृते भागे नागः पुष्पेण वामनः ॥॥। 38 ॥
2.10.m:
And on seven-cubit poles one should place banners / white, red, white, [and] yellow in due order; / in the cardinal directions, the setting up of archways and the wrapping of the archways
should be done with leaves of milk-trees, flowers, and fruits; / and the measure of an archway is declared to be six cubits.
In height, O Rāma, it should be known as two [cubits] equal to the breadth; / Garuḍa, a palmyra tree, a makara, and an ṛṣya deer in due order
one should place in the middle, above the archways, [as well as] the Dānavas; / one should place the hosts of deities endowed with characteristics upon the ear-tips,
with weapons, with banners, and Śatakratu with an umbrella; / and one should prepare the arrangement of the elephants of the quarters with medicinal herbs.
On the petal of Śakra, the wise man should place Airāvaṇa with parched grain; / on the southeast petal he should place the elephant Padma made of flowers.
Puṣpadanta, the southern elephant, should be made with priyaṅgu grains; / and in the southwest quarter the elephant Vāmana with flowers.
