2.11.m:
sleeping on the ground, on the second day having bathed with water poured through a cow's horn / and having sat down in an auspicious place, [he should draw] a sacred diagram.
There he should set out an eight-petaled lotus with auspicious pigments. / In the middle of its pericarp, he should worship the Sun with red
sandalwood, with perfumes, garlands, and ointments, / with foods to chew, eat, and drink, and with incense and lamps.
Having thus performed the worship of the granter of all desires, / he should eat at night, O knower of dharma, having abandoned all other work.
Using his teeth as a mortar, having performed the observance for a year, / at the conclusion of the observance a sacrificial fee must be given to brahmins according to his capacity.
Likewise, a feeding of twice-born [men] should be performed, largely with the three sweets. / Sleeping on the ground constantly that [night], he should again become so.
This excellent son-bestowing observance has been declared to you by me, destroying sins; / this worship of the best of gods, O Rāma, is also said to remove all diseases.

2.55
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
प्रोष्ठपद्यामतीतायां कृष्णपक्षाष्टमी तु या ॥
सोपवासो नरस्तस्यां योषिद्वा तनयार्थिनी ॥1 ॥
स्नाता सरसि धर्मज्ञ तोये चाप्यथ सारसे ॥
पूजनं वासुदेवस्य यथा कुर्यात्तथा शृणु ॥ 2 ॥
घृतप्रस्थेन गोविन्दं स्नापयित्वा जगद्गुरुम् ॥
क्षौद्रेण च ततः पश्चाद्दध्ना च स्नपयेत्ततः ॥ 3 ॥
क्षीरेण स्नपनं कृत्वा ततः पश्चाद्विवक्षितम् ॥
सर्वौषधैश्च गन्धैश्च सर्वबीजफलैस्तथा ॥ 4 ॥
स्नापयित्वानुलिप्येत चन्दनागुरुकुङ्कुमैः ॥
कर्पूरेण तथा राम तथा जातीफलैः शुभैः ॥ 5 ॥
ततः कालोद्भवैः पुष्पैः पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम् ॥
धूपं चागुरुणा दत्त्वा कृत्वा नैवेद्यमुत्तमम् ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
विशेषाद्गोरसप्रायं पुन्नागैरन्वितैः फलैः ॥
पौरुषेण च सूक्तेन हुत्वा चानन्तरं घृतम् ॥ 7 ॥

2.55 / Puṣkara said: / When the full-moon day of Bhādrapada has passed, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, / a man who is fasting, or a woman desiring a son,
having bathed in a pool, O knower of dharma, or in lotus water— / hear how one should perform the worship of Vāsudeva:
Having bathed Govinda, the teacher of the world, with a prastha of ghee, / and then with honey, one should then bathe [him] with curds;
having bathed [him] with milk, then after that as desired, / with all medicinal herbs, with perfumes, and with all seeds and fruits;
and having bathed him, one should anoint him with sandalwood, agallochum, and saffron, / with camphor, O Rāma, and with auspicious nutmegs.
Then having worshipped Janārdana with seasonal flowers, / having offered incense with agallochum, and having made an excellent food offering,
especially consisting mostly of milk products accompanied by punnāga fruits, / and having then offered an oblation of ghee with the Puruṣasūkta,

पुत्रार्थं प्राशनं कुर्यात्फलैः पुन्नामभिः शुभैः ॥

2.11.m:
a śūdra or a woman, having offered oblations to the teacher of the world by his name, / should give vessels of barley, and gold at the Phalguni [constellation].
For the sake of a son, one should consume auspicious fruits bearing masculine names, / and, if desiring a daughter, [fruits] bearing feminine names; then having eaten as desired,
one desiring a son obtains sons and everything desired. / One should offer sacrificial food to the god of gods and adorn the ground.
Having performed this observance for a year, one obtains the desired object; / one desiring a son obtains sons and all desired things.
Even though this excellent observance for obtaining a son has been proclaimed to you by me as constant in dharma, / nonetheless, through its performance, men in the world obtain all desires.

कुक्कुटा बर्हिणः श्रेष्ठास्तिक्ता गोधूमशालयः ॥
हिता जठरिणां भोज्ये यवगोधूमशालयः ॥14 ॥
2.12.m: Cocks and peacocks are best; bitters, wheat, and rice; / for those suffering from abdominal enlargements (udara), barley, wheat, and rice are wholesome for eating;

2.12.s:
mudgāḥ kulatthāḥ kaulāni jāṅgalā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ ..
paṭolanimbadhānyāstu śuṣkamūlakasaindhavaiḥ .. 15 ..
2.12.d:
मुद्गाः कुलत्थाः कौलानि जाङ्गला मृगपक्षिणः ॥
पटोलनिम्बधान्यास्तु शुष्कमूलकसैन्धवैः ॥ 15 ॥
2.12.m: Mung beans, horse gram, wild jujubes, and beasts and birds of arid lands; / pointed gourd, neem, coriander, along with dried radish and rock salt;

2.12.s:
mātuluṅgarasā jātihiṅguvṛkṣāmlavetasaiḥ ..
āhāraṃ jaṭhare yuktyā yathādoṣaṃ prakalpayet.. 16 ..
2.12.d:
मातुलुङ्गरसा जातिहिङ्गुवृक्षाम्लवेतसैः ॥
आहारं जठरे युक्त्या यथादोषं प्रकल्पयेत्॥ 16 ॥
2.12.m: With citron juice, jasmine, asafoetida, garcinia, and cane reed, / one should carefully arrange the diet in abdominal enlargements according to the doshas.

2.12.s:
kuṣṭhināṃ ca tathā śastaṃ pānārthe khadirodakam..
masūramudgau yūṣārthe bhojye jīrṇāśca śālayaḥ .. 17 ..
2.12.d:
कुष्ठिनां च तथा शस्तं पानार्थे खदिरोदकम्॥
मसूरमुद्गौ यूषार्थे भोज्ये जीर्णाश्च शालयः ॥ 17 ॥
2.12.m: And likewise for those afflicted with skin diseases (kuṣṭha), khadira water is praised for drinking; / lentils and mung beans for soup, and aged rice for meals;

2.12.s:
nimbaparpaṭakau śākau chāgalānāṃ tathā rasaḥ ..
viḍaṅgaṃ maricaṃ śuṇṭhī kuṣṭhaṃ rodhraṃ sasarjikam.. 18 ..
2.12.d:
निम्बपर्पटकौ शाकौ छागलानां तथा रसः ॥
विडङ्गं मरिचं शुण्ठी कुष्ठं रोध्रं ससर्जिकम्॥ 18 ॥
2.12.m: Neem and parpaṭaka as greens, and likewise the broth of goats; / false black pepper, black pepper, dry ginger, costus, lodhra, along with natron;

2.12.s:
manaḥśilaiḥ kṛto lepaḥ kuṣṭhahā mūtrapeṣitaḥ ..
apūpasaktukulmāṣavājyādyā mehināṃ hitāḥ .. 19 ..
2.12.d:
मनःशिलैः कृतो लेपः कुष्ठहा मूत्रपेषितः ॥
अपूपसक्तुकुल्माषवाज्याद्या मेहिनां हिताः ॥ 19 ॥
2.12.m: An ointment made of realgar ground with urine destroys skin disease (kuṣṭha). / Cakes, roasted barley flour, boiled pulse, preparations of barley, and the like are beneficial for those suffering from urinary disease (meha);

2.12.s:
yavānnavikṛtirmudgāḥ kulatthājīrṇaśālayaḥ ..
tiktarūkṣāṇi śākāni tiktāni haritāni ca .. 2.56.20 ..
2.12.d:
यवान्नविकृतिर्मुद्गाः कुलत्थाजीर्णशालयः ॥
तिक्तरूक्षाणि शाकानि तिक्तानि हरितानि च ॥ 2.56.20 ॥
2.12.m: Barley preparations, mung beans, horse gram, aged rice, / bitter and unctuous greens, both bitter and fresh;

2.12.s:
tilāni tilaśigrurvā bibhīteṅgudajāni tu ..
anabhiṣyandi yaccānyadbhojane tatpraśasyate .. 21 ...
2.12.d:
तिलानि तिलशिग्रुर्वा बिभीतेङ्गुदजानि तु ॥
अनभिष्यन्दि यच्चान्यद्भोजने तत्प्रशस्यते ॥ 21 ॥।
2.12.m: Sesame, or sesame with moringa, and products of baheda and inguda; / and whatever other food is non-obstructive is praised in eating.

2.12.s:
mudgāḥ sayavagodhūmā dhānyaṃ varṣasthitaṃ ca yat ..
jāṅgālasvarasaḥ prokto bhojane rājayakṣmiṇām.. 22..
2.12.d:
मुद्गाः सयवगोधूमा धान्यं वर्षस्थितं च यत् ॥
जाङ्गालस्वरसः प्रोक्तो भोजने राजयक्ष्मिणाम्॥ 22॥
2.12.m: Mung beans with barley and wheat, and grain that has stood for a year, / and pure juice of wild arid-zone game is declared for the food of those with consumption (rājayakṣman);

2.12.s:
kulatthamudgakālābuśuṣkamūlakajāṅgalaiḥ. ..
yūṣairvā vāṣkiraiḥ snigdhairdadhidāḍimasādhitaiḥ .. 23 ..
2.12.d:
कुलत्थमुद्गकालाबुशुष्कमूलकजाङ्गलैः॥।
यूषैर्वा वाष्किरैः स्निग्धैर्दधिदाडिमसाधितैः ॥ 23 ॥
2.12.m: With horse gram, mung beans, bottle gourd, dried radish, and arid-zone game; / or with soups of birds, unctuous and prepared with curd and pomegranate;

2.12.s:
mātuluṅgarasakṣaudradrākṣāvyoṣādisaṃskṛtaiḥ ..
yavagodhūmaśālyannairbhojayecchāvasaṃ param .. 24 ...
2.12.d:
मातुलुङ्गरसक्षौद्रद्राक्षाव्योषादिसंस्कृतैः ॥
यवगोधूमशाल्यन्नैर्भोजयेच्छावसं परम् ॥ 24 ॥।
2.12.m: Refined with citron juice, honey, grapes, the three pungents, and the like, / one should feed him meals of barley, wheat, and rice, which is superior in consumption (kṣaya).

2.12.s:
daśamūlaphalārāsnākulatthairupasādhitaiḥ ..
payovyūṣarasakvāthaḥ śvāsahikkānivāraṇaḥ .. 25 ..
2.12.d:
दशमूलफलारास्नाकुलत्थैरुपसाधितैः ॥
पयोव्यूषरसक्वाथः श्वासहिक्कानिवारणः ॥ 25 ॥
2.12.m: A decoction of milk and peppery soup prepared with the ten roots, / fruits, rāsnā, and horse gram dispels dyspnea and hiccups.

2.12.s:
śuṣkamūlakakaulatthamaudgajāṃgalajai rasaiḥ ..
yavagodhūmaśālyannaṃ jīrṇāśoṃ'śaṃ samācaret .. 26 ..
2.12.d:
शुष्कमूलककौलत्थमौद्गजांगलजै रसैः ॥
यवगोधूमशाल्यन्नं जीर्णाशोंऽशं समाचरेत् ॥ 26 ॥
2.12.m: With dried radish, horse gram, mung beans, and broths from arid-zone game, / one should consume a food of barley, wheat, and rice in aged piles (arśas).

2.12.s:
jīrṇa pakvarasaṃ śīdhumārdvīkām̐stvatha vā pibet ..
śothavānsaguḍāṃ pathyāṃ khādedvā guḍalāvanam .. .. 27 ..
2.12.d:
जीर्ण पक्वरसं शीधुमार्द्वीकाम्̐स्त्वथ वा पिबेत् ॥
शोथवान्सगुडां पथ्यां खादेद्वा गुडलावनम् ॥ ॥ 27 ॥
2.12.m: Or one should drink aged fermented juice, rum, or grape wine; / one having swelling should eat chebulic myrobalan with jaggery, or jaggery with salt.

2.12.s:
citraṃ vicitrakaṃ cobhau grahaṇīroganāśanau ..
purāṇayavagodhūmaśālayo jāṅgalaṃ rasam .. 28 ..
2.12.d:
चित्रं विचित्रकं चोभौ ग्रहणीरोगनाशनौ ॥
पुराणयवगोधूमशालयो जाङ्गलं रसम् ॥ 28 ॥
2.12.m: Plumbago and white plumbago both destroy malabsorption disorders (grahaṇī); / aged barley, wheat, and rice, and the broth of arid-zone game;

2.12.s:
mudgāmalakakharjūramṛdvīkābadarāṇi ca ..
madhusarpiḥpayastakraṃ nimbaparpaṭakau vṛṣam .. 29 ..
2.12.d:
मुद्गामलकखर्जूरमृद्वीकाबदराणि च ॥
मधुसर्पिःपयस्तक्रं निम्बपर्पटकौ वृषम् ॥ 29 ॥
2.12.m: Mung beans, emblic myrobalan, dates, grapes, and jujubes, / honey, clarified butter, milk, buttermilk, neem, parpaṭaka, and vāśā;

2.12.s:
takravṛddhyānuśasyante satataṃ vātarogiṇām ..
hṛdrogiṇe pradātavyaṃ prayatnena virecanam ..2.56.30..
2.12.d:
तक्रवृद्ध्यानुशस्यन्ते सततं वातरोगिणाम् ॥
हृद्रोगिणे प्रदातव्यं प्रयत्नेन विरेचनम् ॥2.56.30॥
2.12.m: With increasing buttermilk, they are constantly praised for those suffering from vāta disorders. / To one suffering from heart disease, purgation should be given with care;

2.12.s:
pippalīnāṃ prayogaśca pramṛte dharmiṇastathā ..
cakāra nāḍī śīdhūni yuktā ca śiśirāmbhasā .. 31 ..
2.12.d:
पिप्पलीनां प्रयोगश्च प्रमृते धर्मिणस्तथा ॥
चकार नाडी शीधूनि युक्ता च शिशिराम्भसा ॥ 31 ॥
2.12.m: And the application of long pepper [is recommended] likewise when [a person] is overwhelmed. / One should prepare stalk-liquors, combined with cold water;

2.12.s:
yuktasauvarcalājākṣimatha śastaṃ madātyaye ..
sakṣaudrapayasā lākṣāṃ pibeta kṣatavānnaraḥ .. 32 ..
2.12.d:
युक्तसौवर्चलाजाक्षिमथ शस्तं मदात्यये ॥
सक्षौद्रपयसा लाक्षां पिबेत क्षतवान्नरः ॥ 32 ॥
2.12.m: Soothed with sochal salt and goat's milk, [it is] praised in alcohol intoxication; / a man with chest wounds should drink lac with honey and milk.

2.12.s:
kṣayaṃ māṃsarasāhāro vahnisaṃrakṣaṇājjayet ..
śālayo bhojane śaktā nīvārakalamādayaḥ .. 33 ..
2.12.d:
क्षयं मांसरसाहारो वह्निसंरक्षणाज्जयेत् ॥
शालयो भोजने शक्ता नीवारकलमादयः ॥ 33 ॥
2.12.m: Taking a diet of meat broth, one should conquer emaciation by protecting the digestive fire; / rices such as nīvāra, kalama, and the like are capable for food.

2.12.s:
yavānnavikṛtirmāṃsaṃ śākaṃ sauvarcalaṃ sudhīḥ ..
pathyaṃ tathaiva tāsāṃ ca maṇḍaṃ takraṃ ca vāruṇī .. 34 ..
2.12.d:
यवान्नविकृतिर्मांसं शाकं सौवर्चलं सुधीः ॥
पथ्यं तथैव तासां च मण्डं तक्रं च वारुणी ॥ 34 ॥
2.12.m: Barley preparations, meat, the wise person takes sochal greens; / that is wholesome, and likewise the scum, buttermilk, and distilled spirit for them;

2.12.s:
mustābhyāsastathā lepaḥ citrakeṇa haridrayā ..
yavānnavikṛtiḥ śālirvāstukī ca suvarcalam .. 35 ..
2.12.d:
मुस्ताभ्यासस्तथा लेपः चित्रकेण हरिद्रया ॥
यवान्नविकृतिः शालिर्वास्तुकी च सुवर्चलम् ॥ 35 ॥
2.12.m: The regular use of nut grass, likewise an ointment with plumbago and turmeric; / barley preparations, rice, bathua, and suvarcalā;

2.12.s:
trapusī cārugodhūmāḥ kṣīrekṣughṛtasaṃyutāḥ ..
mūtrakṛcche ca śastāḥ syuḥ pāne maṇḍasurādayaḥ ... 36 ..
2.12.d:
त्रपुसी चारुगोधूमाः क्षीरेक्षुघृतसंयुताः ॥
मूत्रकृच्छे च शस्ताः स्युः पाने मण्डसुरादयः ॥। 36 ॥
2.12.m: Cucumber and fine wheat, accompanied by milk, sugarcane [juice], and ghee; / and scum, beer, and the like are praised for drink in dysuria;

2.12.s:
lājā saktu tathā kṣaudraṃ śālyaṃ māṃsaparūṣakam ..
vṛntākālābuśikhinaśchardighnāḥ pānakāni ca .. .. 37 ..
2.12.d:
लाजा सक्तु तथा क्षौद्रं शाल्यं मांसपरूषकम् ॥
वृन्ताकालाबुशिखिनश्छर्दिघ्नाः पानकानि च ॥ ॥ 37 ॥
2.12.m: Parched grain, barley flour, and honey, rice, meat, and phalsa; / eggplant, bottle gourd, peacocks, and syrups destroy vomiting.

2.12.s:
śālyannaṃ toyapayasī kevaloṣṇaśrite'pi vā ..
tṛṣṇāghnā mustaguḍayorgulikā vā mukhe dhṛtā .. 38 ..
2.12.d:
शाल्यन्नं तोयपयसी केवलोष्णश्रितेऽपि वा ॥
तृष्णाघ्ना मुस्तगुडयोर्गुलिका वा मुखे धृता ॥ 38 ॥
2.12.m: Rice meal, water and milk, or plain hot boiled [water], / or a pill of nut grass and jaggery held in the mouth destroys thirst.

2.12.s:
yavānnavikṛtiryūṣaṃ śuṣkamūlakajaṃ tathā ..
śākaṃ paṭolavetrāśramūrustambhavināśanam .. 39 ..
2.12.d:
यवान्नविकृतिर्यूषं शुष्कमूलकजं तथा ॥
शाकं पटोलवेत्राश्रमूरुस्तम्भविनाशनम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.12.m: A dish made of barley, soup of dried radish, / greens of pointed gourd and cane-shoot destroy stiffness of the thighs (ūrustambha);

2.12.s:
muktāḍhakamasūrāṇāmatīrairjāṅgalaistathā ..
sasaindhavaghṛtadrākṣāśuṇṭhyāmalakolajaiḥ .. 2.56.40 ..
2.12.d:
मुक्ताढकमसूराणामतीरैर्जाङ्गलैस्तथा ॥
ससैन्धवघृतद्राक्षाशुण्ठ्यामलकोलजैः ॥ 2.56.40 ॥
2.12.m: With pigeon peas, lentils, and uninhibited game of arid lands, / with rock salt, ghee, grapes, dried ginger, and emblic myrobalan;

2.12.s:
yūṣaiḥ purāṇagodhūmayavaśālyannamabhyaset ..
visarpaṃ sasitākṣaudramṛdvīkādāḍimodaraḥ .. 41 ..
2.12.d:
यूषैः पुराणगोधूमयवशाल्यन्नमभ्यसेत् ॥
विसर्पं ससिताक्षौद्रमृद्वीकादाडिमोदरः ॥ 41 ॥
2.12.m: With soups, one should regularly take food of aged wheat, barley, and rice. / In erysipelas (visarpa), [food mixed] with sugar, honey, grapes, and pomegranate is wholesome;

2.12.s:
raktaṣaṣṭikagodhūmayavamudgādivallaghu ..
kācamācī ca vetrāgraṃ vāstukaṃ ca suvarcalā .. 42 ..
2.12.d:
रक्तषष्टिकगोधूमयवमुद्गादिवल्लघु ॥
काचमाची च वेत्राग्रं वास्तुकं च सुवर्चला ॥ 42 ॥
2.12.m: Light [diet] such as red rice, ṣaṣṭika, wheat, barley, and mung beans, / and black nightshade, cane-shoots, bathua, and suvarcalā.

2.12.s:
vātaśoṣitanāśāya toyaṃ śastaṃ sitā madhu ..
nāsāroge ca sahitaṃ ghṛtadūrvāprasādhitam .. 43 ..
2.12.d:
वातशोषितनाशाय तोयं शस्तं सिता मधु ॥
नासारोगे च सहितं घृतदूर्वाप्रसाधितम् ॥ 43 ॥
2.12.m: Water with sugar and honey is commended for destroying [afflictions caused by] drying from wind, / and in nasal diseases, [it is applied] together with ghee prepared with dūrvā grass.

2.12.s:
bhṛṅgarājarase siddhe tailaṃ dhātrīraso'pi vā ..
na syātsarvāmayeṣviṣṭaṃ mūrdhajatrūdbhaveṣvatha .. 44 ..
2.12.d:
भृङ्गराजरसे सिद्धे तैलं धात्रीरसोऽपि वा ॥
न स्यात्सर्वामयेष्विष्टं मूर्धजत्रूद्भवेष्वथ ॥ 44 ॥
2.12.m: Oil prepared with the juice of bhṛṅgarāja or with the juice of āmalakī / is not unwholesome, [nay, it is] desired in all diseases arising in the head and above the collarbones.

2.12.s:
śītatoyānvapatanaṃ tilānāṃ rāma bhakṣaṇam ..
dvijadārḍhyakaraṃ proktaṃ tathā puṣṭikaraṃ śubham .. 45 ..
2.12.d:
शीततोयान्वपतनं तिलानां राम भक्षणम् ॥
द्विजदार्ढ्यकरं प्रोक्तं तथा पुष्टिकरं शुभम् ॥ 45 ॥
2.12.m: Pouring cold water [over oneself] and the eating of sesame seeds, O Rāma, / is said to strengthen the teeth and likewise to be auspicious and nourishing.

2.12.s:
gaṇḍūṣastilatailena dvijadārḍhyakaraḥ paraḥ ..
viḍaṅgacūrṇaṃ gomūtraṃ sarvatra kṛmināśanam .. 46 ..
2.12.d:
गण्डूषस्तिलतैलेन द्विजदार्ढ्यकरः परः ॥
विडङ्गचूर्णं गोमूत्रं सर्वत्र कृमिनाशनम् ॥ 46 ॥
2.12.m: Gargling with sesame oil is supreme for strengthening the teeth. / Viḍaṅga powder with cow's urine destroys worms everywhere.

2.12.s:
dhātrīphalānyathājyaṃ ca śirolepanamuttamam..
śirorogavināśāya snigdhaśītaṃ ca bhojanam..47..
2.12.d:
धात्रीफलान्यथाज्यं च शिरोलेपनमुत्तमम्॥
शिरोरोगविनाशाय स्निग्धशीतं च भोजनम्॥47॥
2.12.m: Āmalakī fruits and ghee make an excellent paste for the head. / For the destruction of head diseases, one's food should be unctuous and cooling.

2.12.s:
tailaṃ vā vasti mūtraṃ vā karṇapūraṇamuttamam ..
karṇaśūlavināśāya śuddhaṃ tailaṃ niṣecayet .. 48 ..
2.12.d:
तैलं वा वस्ति मूत्रं वा कर्णपूरणमुत्तमम् ॥
कर्णशूलविनाशाय शुद्धं तैलं निषेचयेत् ॥ 48 ॥
2.12.m: Oil, or an enema, or urine is excellent for filling the ear. / To destroy earaches, one should pour in pure oil.

2.12.s:
giribhṛccandanaṃ mālyaṃ mālatīkālikāstathā ..
saṃyojya yākṛtāvartiḥ kṣatacakraharītusā ..49 ..
2.12.d:
गिरिभृच्चन्दनं माल्यं मालतीकालिकास्तथा ॥
संयोज्य याकृतावर्तिः क्षतचक्रहरीतुसा ॥49 ॥
2.12.m: Mountain-borne sandalwood, a garland, and buds of the mālatī jasmine— / having combined these, a wick made with liver removes ocular injury.

2.12.s:
vyoṣaṃ triphalayāyuktaṃ surūkaṃ ca rasāñjanam ..
sarvākṣirogaśamanaṃ tathā caiva rasāñjanam .. 2.56.50 ..
2.12.d:
व्योषं त्रिफलयायुक्तं सुरूकं च रसाञ्जनम् ॥
सर्वाक्षिरोगशमनं तथा चैव रसाञ्जनम् ॥ 2.56.50 ॥
2.12.m: The three pungents joined with the three myrobalans, surūka, and rasāñjana— / likewise, rasāñjana soothes all eye diseases.

2.12.s:
ājyabhṛṣṭaṃ śilāpiṣṭarothakāñjikasaindhavaiḥ ..
āścyotanavināśāya sarvarogāmayeṣu ca .. 51 ..
2.12.d:
आज्यभृष्टं शिलापिष्टरोथकाञ्जिकसैन्धवैः ॥
आश्च्योतनविनाशाय सर्वरोगामयेषु च ॥ 51 ॥
2.12.m: Fried in ghee and ground on a stone with rotha, sour gruel, and rock salt, / [this is used] for the destruction of eye-drops and in all diseases and afflictions.

2.12.s:
giribhṛccandanairlepo bahirlepasya śasyate ..
netrāmayavighātārthaṃ triphalāṃ śīlayetsadā .. 52..
2.12.d:
गिरिभृच्चन्दनैर्लेपो बहिर्लेपस्य शस्यते ॥
नेत्रामयविघातार्थं त्रिफलां शीलयेत्सदा ॥ 52॥
2.12.m: An external plaster of mountain-borne sandalwood is praised. / For the destruction of eye diseases, one should always use the three myrobalans.

2.12.s:
rātrau tu madhusarpibhyāṃ dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ ..
śatāvare rase siddhau vṛṣyau kṣīraghṛtau smṛtau..53..
2.12.d:
रात्रौ तु मधुसर्पिभ्यां दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः ॥
शतावरे रसे सिद्धौ वृष्यौ क्षीरघृतौ स्मृतौ॥53॥
2.12.m: At night, however, one wishing to live a long life [takes them] with honey and ghee. / Milk and ghee prepared in the juice of śatāvarī are traditionally considered aphrodisiacs.

2.12.s:
kalaviṅkāni māṣāśca vṛṣau kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā ..
āyuṣyā triphalā caiva pūrvavanmadhukānvitā .. 54 ..
2.12.d:
कलविङ्कानि माषाश्च वृषौ क्षीरं घृतं तथा ॥
आयुष्या त्रिफला चैव पूर्ववन्मधुकान्विता ॥ 54 ॥
2.12.m: Sparrows and black gram are aphrodisiacs, as are milk and ghee. / The three myrobalans promote longevity, combined with licorice as before.

2.12.s:
madhukāyorajopetā valīpalitanāśinī ..
vacasiddhaṃ ghṛtaṃ rāma tadā bhūtavināśanam .. 55 ..
2.12.d:
मधुकायोरजोपेता वलीपलितनाशिनी ॥
वचसिद्धं घृतं राम तदा भूतविनाशनम् ॥ 55 ॥
2.12.m: Joined with licorice and iron filings, it destroys wrinkles and gray hair. / Ghee prepared with calamus, O Rāma, then destroys evil spirits.

2.12.s:
kaṇṭhe buddhipradaṃ caiva tathā sarvārthasādhakam ..
valgakalkakaṣāyeṇa siddhamabhyañjanaṃ hitam..56..
2.12.d:
कण्ठे बुद्धिप्रदं चैव तथा सर्वार्थसाधकम् ॥
वल्गकल्ककषायेण सिद्धमभ्यञ्जनं हितम्॥56॥
2.12.m: It grants intellect to the throat and accomplishes all aims. / An inunction prepared with the decoction and paste of valga is beneficial.

2.12.s:
rāsnā sahacarairvāpi tailaṃ vātavikāriṇām ..
anabhiṣyandi yaccānyattadvraṇeṣu praśasyate .. 57 ..
2.12.d:
रास्ना सहचरैर्वापि तैलं वातविकारिणाम् ॥
अनभिष्यन्दि यच्चान्यत्तद्व्रणेषु प्रशस्यते ॥ 57 ॥
2.12.m: Oil with rāsnā or sahacara is for those afflicted with wind disorders. / Whatever else does not cause clogging of the channels is praised for ulcers.

2.12.s:
pakvasya ca tathā bhedaṃ nimbaśīlaṃ ca ropaṇe ..
tathā tasyopacāraśca balikarmārthiśeṣataḥ .. 58 ..
2.12.d:
पक्वस्य च तथा भेदं निम्बशीलं च रोपणे ॥
तथा तस्योपचारश्च बलिकर्मार्थिशेषतः ॥ 58 ॥
2.12.m: Likewise, the incision of what is ripe, and the habitual use of neem for healing; / and its treatment [should be done] especially by one seeking the ritual of oblations.

2.12.s:
sūtikā ca tathā rakṣā vraṇināṃ tu sadā hitā ..
jaṅgame viṣadaṃśe tu dātavyaṃ sthāvaraṃ viṣam .. ..59..
2.12.d:
सूतिका च तथा रक्षा व्रणिनां तु सदा हिता ॥
जङ्गमे विषदंशे तु दातव्यं स्थावरं विषम् ॥ ॥59॥
2.12.m: The protection [given to] a woman in childbed is likewise always beneficial for those with wounds. / In a bite from mobile venom, immobile poison should be administered.

2.12.s:
sthāvare sarpadaṣṭasya hitaṃ māṃsasya bhakṣaṇam ..
bhakṣaṇaṃ nimbapatrāṇāṃ sarpadaṣṭasya bheṣajam .. 2.56.60 ..
2.12.d:
स्थावरे सर्पदष्टस्य हितं मांसस्य भक्षणम् ॥
भक्षणं निम्बपत्राणां सर्पदष्टस्य भेषजम् ॥ 2.56.60 ॥
2.12.m: In immobile [poison], the eating of meat is beneficial for one bitten by a snake. / The eating of neem leaves is a remedy for one bitten by a snake.

2.12.s:
vandhyākārkoṭajaṃ mūlaṃ chāgamūtrābhibhāvitam ..
nasyaṃ kāñcikasaṃpiṣṭaṃ viṣavegavināśanam ..61..
2.12.d:
वन्ध्याकार्कोटजं मूलं छागमूत्राभिभावितम् ॥
नस्यं काञ्चिकसंपिष्टं विषवेगविनाशनम् ॥61॥
2.12.m: The root of sterile kārkoṭa infused with goat's urine, / ground with sour gruel and used as a nasal drop, destroys the onset of poison.

2.12.s:
bandhanāddūṣaṇaṃ chedadāhasrāvāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
pūrvadaṣṭasya pāne ca hṛdayāvaraṇa ghṛtam .. ..62..
2.12.d:
बन्धनाद्दूषणं छेददाहस्रावाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
पूर्वदष्टस्य पाने च हृदयावरण घृतम् ॥ ॥62॥
2.12.m: Vitiation through tying, incision, cautery, and bloodletting are prescribed. / For one bitten long before, drinking ghee covers the heart.

2.12.s:
tālanimbadalaṃ keśā jīrṇacailaṃ yavā ghṛtam ..
dhūpo vṛścikaviddhasya śikhipatraṃ ghṛtena vā..63..
2.12.d:
तालनिम्बदलं केशा जीर्णचैलं यवा घृतम् ॥
धूपो वृश्चिकविद्धस्य शिखिपत्रं घृतेन वा॥63॥
2.12.m: Palmyra leaves, neem leaves, hair, old cloth, barley, and ghee: / this is a fumigation for one stung by a scorpion, or peacock feathers with ghee.

2.12.s:
arkakṣīreṇa saṃpiṣṭaṃ lepabījaṃ palāśajam..
vṛścikārttasya kṛṣṇā vā śirīṣaphalasaṃyutā .. 64 ..
2.12.d:
अर्कक्षीरेण संपिष्टं लेपबीजं पलाशजम्॥
वृश्चिकार्त्तस्य कृष्णा वा शिरीषफलसंयुता ॥ 64 ॥
2.12.m: A paste of palāśa seeds ground with the milky sap of arka, / or long pepper joined with the fruit of śirīṣa, [is used] for one afflicted by a scorpion.

2.12.s:
tilakāsphoṭayordūnaṃ girikarṇyāstilasya ca ..
śarkarāmadhusarpīṃṣi pānamākhuviṣāpaham .. ..65..
2.12.d:
तिलकास्फोटयोर्दूनं गिरिकर्ण्यास्तिलस्य च ॥
शर्करामधुसर्पींषि पानमाखुविषापहम् ॥ ॥65॥
2.12.m: Pounded tilaka and āsphoṭā, girikarṇī and sesame, / with sugar, honey, and ghee, as a drink, removes rat poison.

2.12.s:
ārkakṣīraṃ tilāstailaṃ palalaṃ ca guru samam ..
pānājjayati durvāramaviṣaṃ śīghrameva ca..66..
2.12.d:
आर्कक्षीरं तिलास्तैलं पललं च गुरु समम् ॥
पानाज्जयति दुर्वारमविषं शीघ्रमेव च॥66॥
2.12.m: Milky sap of arka, sesame seeds, oil, and heavy ground sesame paste in equal parts / quickly conquers unstoppable poison through drinking.

2.12.s:
pītvā mūlaṃ trivṛttulyaṃ taṇḍulīyasya sarpiṣā..
sarpakīṭaviṣāṇyāśu jayatyatibalānyapi .. 67 ..
2.12.d:
पीत्वा मूलं त्रिवृत्तुल्यं तण्डुलीयस्य सर्पिषा॥
सर्पकीटविषाण्याशु जयत्यतिबलान्यपि ॥ 67 ॥
2.12.m: Having drunk the root of taṇḍulīya equal [in measure] to trivṛt with ghee, / one swiftly conquers even extremely potent snake and insect poisons.

2.12.s:
candanaṃ padmakaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ natāmbūśīrapāṭalāḥ ..
nirguṇḍīśākhiśailūṣalūtāviṣaharo'gadaḥ .. 68 ..
2.12.d:
चन्दनं पद्मकं कुष्ठं नताम्बूशीरपाटलाः ॥
निर्गुण्डीशाखिशैलूषलूताविषहरोऽगदः ॥ 68 ॥
2.12.m: Sandalwood, padmaka, kuṣṭha, nata, ambu, uśīra, pāṭalā, / nirguṇḍī, tree-bark, and śailūṣa: this antidote removes spider poison.

2.12.s:
śirovirecanaṃ śastaṃ guḍanāgarakaṃ dvija ..
nasyakarmaṇi vastau ca tathā bhṛṅge ca bhārgava .. 69 ..
2.12.d:
शिरोविरेचनं शस्तं गुडनागरकं द्विज ॥
नस्यकर्मणि वस्तौ च तथा भृङ्गे च भार्गव ॥ 69 ॥
2.12.m: Purgation of the head with jaggery and dry ginger is praised, O twice-born, / in the procedure of nasal medication, in an enema, and in bhṛṅga, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.12.s:
tailameva paraṃ vidyātsnehapāne tathā ghṛtam ..
svedanīyaḥ paro vahniḥ sitāmbhaḥstambhanaṃ param .. 2.56.70 ..
2.12.d:
तैलमेव परं विद्यात्स्नेहपाने तथा घृतम् ॥
स्वेदनीयः परो वह्निः सिताम्भःस्तम्भनं परम् ॥ 2.56.70 ॥
2.12.m: One should know oil alone to be supreme, and likewise ghee in the drinking of unctuous substances. / Fire is the supreme sweating agent, and cold water is the supreme astringent.

2.12.s:
trivṛddhi recane śreṣṭhā vamane madanaṃ tathā ..
vastirvireko vamanaṃ tailaṃ sarpistathā madhu ..71..
2.12.d:
त्रिवृद्धि रेचने श्रेष्ठा वमने मदनं तथा ॥
वस्तिर्विरेको वमनं तैलं सर्पिस्तथा मधु ॥71॥
2.12.m: Trivṛt is indeed best for purgation, and madana for emesis; / enema, purgation, and emesis [rely on] oil, ghee, and honey.

2.12.s:
raktapitte balā rāsnā krameṇa paramauṣadham ..
śārīramānasāgraṃ tu sahajā vyādhayo matāḥ .. 72 ..
2.12.d:
रक्तपित्ते बला रास्ना क्रमेण परमौषधम् ॥
शारीरमानसाग्रं तु सहजा व्याधयो मताः ॥ 72 ॥
2.12.m: In bleeding disorders, balā and rāsnā are, in order, the supreme medicine. / Diseases are considered innate, and foremost among bodily and mental ones.

2.12.s:
śārīrajvarakuṣṭhādyāḥ krodhādyā mānasā matāḥ ..
āgantavo'bhighātotthāḥ sahajāḥ kṣuttṛṣādayaḥ .. 73 ..
2.12.d:
शारीरज्वरकुष्ठाद्याः क्रोधाद्या मानसा मताः ॥
आगन्तवोऽभिघातोत्थाः सहजाः क्षुत्तृषादयः ॥ 73 ॥
2.12.m: Bodily [diseases] are fever, leprosy, and the like; mental ones are considered anger and the like; / exogenous ones arise from injury; innate ones are hunger, thirst, and the like.

2.12.s:
śārīrāgantunāśāya satataṃ sūryavāsare ..
guḍājyalavaṇopetaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ dvijātaye ..74..
2.12.d:
शारीरागन्तुनाशाय सततं सूर्यवासरे ॥
गुडाज्यलवणोपेतं सहिरण्यं द्विजातये ॥74॥
2.12.m: For the destruction of bodily and exogenous [diseases], constantly on Sunday / [one should give] to a twice-born jaggery, ghee, and salt, together with gold,

2.12.s:
dadyācca dhūpaṃ dharmajña prīṇayecca divākaram ..
ārogyametenāpnoti kāmām̐śca manasepsitān .. 75 ..
2.12.d:
दद्याच्च धूपं धर्मज्ञ प्रीणयेच्च दिवाकरम् ॥
आरोग्यमेतेनाप्नोति कामाम्̐श्च मनसेप्सितान् ॥ 75 ॥
2.12.m: and one should give incense, O knower of dharma, and please the Sun. / Through this, one attains health and the desires wished for in one's mind.

2.12.s:
satataṃ divase cāndre snānamabhyaṅgapūrvakan ..
yaḥ prayacchati viprāya so'pi rogairvimucyate .. ..76 ..
2.12.d:
सततं दिवसे चान्द्रे स्नानमभ्यङ्गपूर्वकन् ॥
यः प्रयच्छति विप्राय सोऽपि रोगैर्विमुच्यते ॥ ॥76 ॥
2.12.m: He who constantly offers a bath preceded by inunction / to a brahmin on Monday is also freed from diseases.

2.12.s:
śanaiścaradine dattvā tailaṃ vipreṣu śaktitaḥ..
nityameva mahābhāga roganāśanamāpnuyāt .. 77 ..
2.12.d:
शनैश्चरदिने दत्त्वा तैलं विप्रेषु शक्तितः॥
नित्यमेव महाभाग रोगनाशनमाप्नुयात् ॥ 77 ॥
2.12.m: Having given oil to brahmins on Saturday according to one's capacity, / O fortunate one, one will permanently attain the destruction of disease.

2.12.s:
āśvinaṃ sakalaṃ māsaṃ pratyahaṃ gorasairdvijān ..
bhojayitvā mahābhāga roganāśanamāpnuyāt ..78..
2.12.d:
आश्विनं सकलं मासं प्रत्यहं गोरसैर्द्विजान् ॥
भोजयित्वा महाभाग रोगनाशनमाप्नुयात् ॥78॥
2.12.m: Having fed twice-born men with milk products every day for the entire month of Āśvina, / O fortunate one, one will attain the destruction of disease.

2.12.s:
snāpayitvā tathā liṅgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
ghṛtena payasā caiva sarvarogairvimucyate .. 79 ..
2.12.d:
स्नापयित्वा तथा लिङ्गं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ॥
घृतेन पयसा चैव सर्वरोगैर्विमुच्यते ॥ 79 ॥
2.12.m: Likewise, having bathed the liṅga of the god of gods, the trident-bearer, / with ghee and milk, one is freed from all diseases.

2.12.s:
gāyatryāvāhayedvidvāndūrvāṃ trimadhunāplutām ..
pūtaśca brāhmaṇāśīrbhiḥ sarvarogairvimucyate .. 2.56.80 ..
2.12.d:
गायत्र्यावाहयेद्विद्वान्दूर्वां त्रिमधुनाप्लुताम् ॥
पूतश्च ब्राह्मणाशीर्भिः सर्वरोगैर्विमुच्यते ॥ 2.56.80 ॥
2.12.m: The wise man should invoke with the Gāyatrī dūrvā grass immersed in the three sweets; / and purified by the blessings of brahmins, he is freed from all diseases.

2.12.s:
yasminbhe vyādhimāpnoti kṛtvā tasya balikriyām ..
bhapūjāvidhinā rāma tasmādrogādvimucyate..81..
2.12.d:
यस्मिन्भे व्याधिमाप्नोति कृत्वा तस्य बलिक्रियाम् ॥
भपूजाविधिना राम तस्माद्रोगाद्विमुच्यते॥81॥
2.12.m: Having performed the offering ritual for the asterism under which one contracts a disease, / in accordance with the rule for worshiping the asterisms, O Rāma, one is freed from that disease.

2.12.s:
kartavyamathavā snānaṃ tathārogyavivardhanam ..
ārogyadāṃ dvitīyāṃ vā pratipadvā bhṛgūttama .. 82 ..
2.12.d:
कर्तव्यमथवा स्नानं तथारोग्यविवर्धनम् ॥
आरोग्यदां द्वितीयां वा प्रतिपद्वा भृगूत्तम ॥ 82 ॥
2.12.m: Or a bath should be performed that increases health; / or on the second or first lunar day that grants health, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,

2.12.s:
kartavyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ vāpi vratamārogyakārakam ..
mānasānāṃ nijānāṃ ca tathā caivāvipattaye ..83 ..
2.12.d:
कर्तव्यं वैष्णवं वापि व्रतमारोग्यकारकम् ॥
मानसानां निजानां च तथा चैवाविपत्तये ॥83 ॥
2.12.m: a Vaiṣṇava observance should also be performed which produces health, / for the non-ruin of mental and innate [faculties].

2.12.s:
śaraṇaṃ devadeveśaṃ vrajeta madhusūdanam ..
sarvagaṃ taṃ jagannāthamajeyaṃ puruṣottamam .. 84 ..
2.12.d:
शरणं देवदेवेशं व्रजेत मधुसूदनम् ॥
सर्वगं तं जगन्नाथमजेयं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥ 84 ॥
2.12.m: One should go for refuge to Madhusūdana, the lord of the gods of gods, / the all-pervading lord of the world, the invincible Puruṣottama.

2.12.s:
stuvannāmasahasreṇa vyādhīnsarvānvyapohati ..
doṣadhātumalādhāraṃ śarīraṃ prāṇināṃ dvija .. 85 ..
2.12.d:
स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण व्याधीन्सर्वान्व्यपोहति ॥
दोषधातुमलाधारं शरीरं प्राणिनां द्विज ॥ 85 ॥
2.12.m: Praising him with the Thousand Names, one drives away all diseases. / The body of living beings, O twice-born, is the receptacle of humors, bodily elements, and waste products.

2.12.s:
vātapittakaphā doṣā dhātavaśca tathā śṛṇu ..
bhuktaṃ pakvāśayādannaṃ dvidhā yāti bhṛgūttama .. 86 ..
2.12.d:
वातपित्तकफा दोषा धातवश्च तथा शृणु ॥
भुक्तं पक्वाशयादन्नं द्विधा याति भृगूत्तम ॥ 86 ॥
2.12.m: Wind, bile, and phlegm are the humors; and listen likewise to the bodily elements: / food that is eaten goes twofold from the organ of digestion, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.

2.12.s:
aṃśenaikena kiṭṭatvaṃ rasatāṃ cāpareṇa ca ..
kiṭṭabhāgo malastatra viṇmūtrasvedadūṣakaḥ .. 87 ..
2.12.d:
अंशेनैकेन किट्टत्वं रसतां चापरेण च ॥
किट्टभागो मलस्तत्र विण्मूत्रस्वेददूषकः ॥ 87 ॥
2.12.m: By one portion it attains the state of waste, and by the other the state of chyle. / The waste portion there is the refuse that fouls feces, urine, and sweat.

2.12.s:
nāsāmalaṃ dehamalaṃ tathā karṇamalaṃ ca yat ..
rasabhāge rasaṃ tatra samyakśoṇitatāṃ vrajet .. 88 ..
2.12.d:
नासामलं देहमलं तथा कर्णमलं च यत् ॥
रसभागे रसं तत्र सम्यक्शोणिततां व्रजेत् ॥ 88 ॥
2.12.m: Nasal excretion, bodily waste, and earwax—all that [is waste]. / In the nutrient fluid portion, the nutrient fluid there properly becomes blood.

2.12.s:
māṃsaṃ raktantato medo medasosthnāṃ ca sambhavaḥ ..
asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukrādrāma tato rasaḥ ..89 ..
2.12.d:
मांसं रक्तन्ततो मेदो मेदसोस्थ्नां च सम्भवः ॥
अस्थ्नो मज्जा ततः शुक्रं शुक्राद्राम ततो रसः ॥89 ॥
2.12.m: From blood comes flesh, from that fat, and from fat arises bone; / from bone marrow, from that semen, and from semen, O Rāma, then comes nutrient fluid.

2.12.s:
sarveṣāmeva dhātūnāṃ sāramojaḥ prakīrtitam ..
deśaṃ sātmyaṃ ca yāṃ śaktiṃ kālaṃ prakṛtimeva ca ..2.56.90 ..
2.12.d:
सर्वेषामेव धातूनां सारमोजः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
देशं सात्म्यं च यां शक्तिं कालं प्रकृतिमेव च ॥2.56.90 ॥
2.12.m: Ojas is proclaimed as the essence of all the bodily elements. / Having understood the region, the suitability, the capacity, the time, and the bodily constitution,

2.12.s:
jñātvā cikitsitaṃ kuryādbheṣajasya tathā balam ..
tithiṃ riktāṃ dineśaṃ ca tathaiva ca kujārkajau.. .. 91 ..
2.12.d:
ज्ञात्वा चिकित्सितं कुर्याद्भेषजस्य तथा बलम् ॥
तिथिं रिक्तां दिनेशं च तथैव च कुजार्कजौ॥ ॥ 91 ॥
2.12.m: as well as the strength of the medicine, one should undertake medical treatment. / [Avoiding] the empty lunar day, the [inauspicious] solar day, and Mars and Saturn,

2.12.s:
dāruṇogrāṇi carkṣāṇi varjayedbheṣaje sadā ..
harigodvijacandrārkasurāgnīnpratipūjya ca.. 92 ..
2.12.d:
दारुणोग्राणि चर्क्षाणि वर्जयेद्भेषजे सदा ॥
हरिगोद्विजचन्द्रार्कसुराग्नीन्प्रतिपूज्य च॥ 92 ॥
2.12.m: one should always avoid cruel and fierce asterisms in administering medicine. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu, cows, the twice-born, the moon, the sun, the gods, and fire,

2.12.s:
śrutvā mantramimaṃ vidvānbheṣajārambhamācaret ..
brahmatryakṣāśvirudrendrabhūcandrārkanalānilāḥ .. 93 ..
2.12.d:
श्रुत्वा मन्त्रमिमं विद्वान्भेषजारम्भमाचरेत् ॥
ब्रह्मत्र्यक्षाश्विरुद्रेन्द्रभूचन्द्रार्कनलानिलाः ॥ 93 ॥
2.12.m: and having recited this mantra, the wise one should commence the medicine: / 'May Brahmā, the Three-eyed [Śiva], the Aśvins, Rudra, Indra, the Earth, the Moon, the Sun, Fire, and Wind,

2.12.s:
ṛṣaya oṣadhigrāmā bhūtasargāśca pāntu te..
rasāyanamivarṣīṇāṃ devānāmamṛtaṃ yathā .. 94 ..
2.12.d:
ऋषय ओषधिग्रामा भूतसर्गाश्च पान्तु ते॥
रसायनमिवर्षीणां देवानाममृतं यथा ॥ 94 ॥
2.12.m: the ṛṣis, the assemblies of medicinal plants, and the classes of beings protect you! / Just as rejuvenation therapy is for the ṛṣis, as ambrosia is for the gods,

2.12.s:
svadhevottamanāgānāṃ bhaiṣajyamidamaśnute ..
vātaśleṣmātmako deśo bahuvṛkṣo bahūdakaḥ .. 95 ..
2.12.d:
स्वधेवोत्तमनागानां भैषज्यमिदमश्नुते ॥
वातश्लेष्मात्मको देशो बहुवृक्षो बहूदकः ॥ 95 ॥
2.12.m: and as svadhā is for the noble nāgas, so may this medicine be effective [for you].' / A region characterized by wind and phlegm has many trees and much water;

2.12.s:
anūpa iti vikhyāto jāṅgalastadvivarjitaḥ ..
kiṃñcidvṛkṣādhiko deśastathā sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..96..
2.12.d:
अनूप इति विख्यातो जाङ्गलस्तद्विवर्जितः ॥
किंञ्चिद्वृक्षाधिको देशस्तथा साधारणः स्मृतः ॥96॥
2.12.m: it is renowned as humid marshland; the arid region is devoid of that. / A region with somewhat more trees is known as ordinary.

2.12.s:
jāṅgalaḥ pittabahulo madhyaḥ sādhāraṇo mataḥ..
rūkṣaśītaścalo vātaḥ pittamuṣṇakaṭudravam .. 97 ..
2.12.d:
जाङ्गलः पित्तबहुलो मध्यः साधारणो मतः॥
रूक्षशीतश्चलो वातः पित्तमुष्णकटुद्रवम् ॥ 97 ॥
2.12.m: The arid region has an abundance of bile; the intermediate is regarded as ordinary. / Wind is dry, cold, and mobile; bile is hot, pungent, and liquid.

2.12.s:
sthirāmlasnigdhamadhuraṃ balāsaṃ ca pracakṣate ..
vṛddhiḥ samānaiḥ sarveṣāṃ viparītairviparyayaḥ .. 98 ..
2.12.d:
स्थिराम्लस्निग्धमधुरं बलासं च प्रचक्षते ॥
वृद्धिः समानैः सर्वेषां विपरीतैर्विपर्ययः ॥ 98 ॥
2.12.m: And phlegm is declared to be stable, sour, unctuous, and sweet. / The increase of all of them is caused by similar [qualities], and the reverse by opposite ones.

2.12.s:
samāḥ svādvamlalavaṇāḥ śleṣmalā vāyunāśanāḥ ..
kaṭutiktakaṣāyāśca vātalāḥ śleṣmanāśanāḥ .. 99 ..
2.12.d:
समाः स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः श्लेष्मला वायुनाशनाः ॥
कटुतिक्तकषायाश्च वातलाः श्लेष्मनाशनाः ॥ 99 ॥
2.12.m: Even, sweet, sour, and salty [tastes] increase phlegm and destroy wind. / Pungent, bitter, and astringent [tastes] increase wind and destroy phlegm.

2.12.s:
kaṭvamlalavaṇā jñeyāstathā pittavivardhanāḥ ..
tiktāḥ svādukaṣāyāśca tathā pittavināśanāḥ .. 2.56.100 ..
2.12.d:
कट्वम्ललवणा ज्ञेयास्तथा पित्तविवर्धनाः ॥
तिक्ताः स्वादुकषायाश्च तथा पित्तविनाशनाः ॥ 2.56.100 ॥
2.12.m: Pungent, sour, and salty [tastes] are to be known as aggravating bile; / bitter, sweet, and astringent [tastes] are likewise pacifiers of bile.

2.12.s:
svabhāvatastathā karma te ca kurvanti bhārgava ..
śiśire ca vasante ca nidāghe ca tathā kramāt .. 101 ..
2.12.d:
स्वभावतस्तथा कर्म ते च कुर्वन्ति भार्गव ॥
शिशिरे च वसन्ते च निदाघे च तथा क्रमात् ॥ 101 ॥
2.12.m: And they perform their action according to their inherent nature, O Bhārgava. / In the cool season, in spring, and in summer, respectively,

2.12.s:
cayaprakopapraśamāstathā pittasya kīrtitāḥ ..
nidāghe vāridā rātre tathā śaradi bhārgava .. 102 ..
2.12.d:
चयप्रकोपप्रशमास्तथा पित्तस्य कीर्तिताः ॥
निदाघे वारिदा रात्रे तथा शरदि भार्गव ॥ 102 ॥
2.12.m: the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of bile are proclaimed. / In summer, during the rainy nights, and in autumn, O Bhārgava,

2.12.s:
cayaprakopapraśamāstathā vātasya kīrtitāḥ ..
cayaprakopapraśamāḥ śleṣmaṇaśca prakīrtitāḥ .. 103 ..
2.12.d:
चयप्रकोपप्रशमास्तथा वातस्य कीर्तिताः ॥
चयप्रकोपप्रशमाः श्लेष्मणश्च प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 103 ॥
2.12.m: the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of wind are proclaimed. / [Likewise,] the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of phlegm are proclaimed.

2.12.s:
saṃvatsaro dvādaśāṅgo māsabhedena kīrtitaḥ ..
dvidhā tu matabhedena bhūya eva prakīrtitaḥ .. 104 ..
2.12.d:
संवत्सरो द्वादशाङ्गो मासभेदेन कीर्तितः ॥
द्विधा तु मतभेदेन भूय एव प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 104 ॥
2.12.m: The year is proclaimed to have twelve limbs according to the division of months; / but it is further proclaimed as twofold according to a division of doctrine.

2.12.s:
ādānaśca visargaśca tatrāpi parikīrtitau ..
varṣādayo visargāśca hemantādyāḥ smṛtāstrayaḥ .. 105 ..
2.12.d:
आदानश्च विसर्गश्च तत्रापि परिकीर्तितौ ॥
वर्षादयो विसर्गाश्च हेमन्ताद्याः स्मृतास्त्रयः ॥ 105 ॥
2.12.m: The period of drawing [heat] and the period of releasing [moisture] are also proclaimed therein; / releasing consists of the three beginning with the rainy season, while [the three] beginning with the early winter are known [as the other].

2.12.s:
meghakāle ca śaradi hemante ca yathākramāt ..
cayaprakopapraśamastathā pittasya kīrtitaḥ .. 106 ..
2.12.d:
मेघकाले च शरदि हेमन्ते च यथाक्रमात् ॥
चयप्रकोपप्रशमस्तथा पित्तस्य कीर्तितः ॥ 106 ॥
2.12.m: In the season of clouds, in autumn, and in winter, respectively, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of bile are declared.

2.12.s:
śiśirādyāstathādānaṃ grīṣmāntā ṛtavastrayaḥ ..
saumyo visargastvādānaṃ cāgneyaṃ parikīrtitam .. 107 ..
2.12.d:
शिशिराद्यास्तथादानं ग्रीष्मान्ता ऋतवस्त्रयः ॥
सौम्यो विसर्गस्त्वादानं चाग्नेयं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 107 ॥
2.12.m: The three seasons beginning with the cool season and ending with summer are the period of drawing; / the period of releasing is lunar, while the period of drawing is proclaimed solar.

2.12.s:
varṣādīnstrīnṛtūnrāma catuḥparyāyagorasān ..
vivardhayettathā tiktakaṣāyakaṭukānkramāt .. 108 ..
2.12.d:
वर्षादीन्स्त्रीनृतून्राम चतुःपर्यायगोरसान् ॥
विवर्धयेत्तथा तिक्तकषायकटुकान्क्रमात् ॥ 108 ॥
2.12.m: During the three seasons beginning with the rainy season, O Rāma, one should increase / milk products in four intervals, and bitter, astringent, and pungent [tastes] in succession.

2.12.s:
yathā rajanyo vardhante balamevaṃ vivardhate ..
kramaśo'tha manuṣyāṇāṃ hīyamānāsu hīyate .. 109 ..
2.12.d:
यथा रजन्यो वर्धन्ते बलमेवं विवर्धते ॥
क्रमशोऽथ मनुष्याणां हीयमानासु हीयते ॥ 109 ॥
2.12.m: Just as the nights grow longer, in the same way the strength / of men gradually increases; when they decrease, it decreases.

2.12.s:
rātribhuktaṃ dinānte tu divasasya tathaiva ca ..
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu kaphapittasamīraṇāḥ .. 2.56.110 ..
2.12.d:
रात्रिभुक्तं दिनान्ते तु दिवसस्य तथैव च ॥
आदिमध्यावसानेषु कफपित्तसमीरणाः ॥ 2.56.110 ॥
2.12.m: What is eaten at night and at the end of day; likewise, of the day / at the beginning, middle, and end, phlegm, bile, and wind [respectively]

2.12.s:
prakopaṃ yānti kopādau kāle yeṣāṃ cayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
prakopāntaraje kāle śamasteṣāṃ prakīrtitaḥ .. 111 ..
2.12.d:
प्रकोपं यान्ति कोपादौ काले येषां चयः स्मृतः ॥
प्रकोपान्तरजे काले शमस्तेषां प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 111 ॥
2.12.m: become aggravated. For those whose accumulation is known to occur at the time of aggravation, / their pacification is proclaimed at the time arising after aggravation.

2.12.s:
atibhojanato rāma tathā cābhojanena ca ..
sarve'pi rogā jāyante vegodīraṇadhāraṇaiḥ .. 112 ..
2.12.d:
अतिभोजनतो राम तथा चाभोजनेन च ॥
सर्वेऽपि रोगा जायन्ते वेगोदीरणधारणैः ॥ 112 ॥
2.12.m: From overeating, O Rāma, and likewise from fasting, / and from suppressing or forcing natural urges, all diseases arise.

2.12.s:
annena kukṣerdvāvaṃśau pānenaikaṃ prapūrayet ..
āśrayaṃ pavanādīnāṃ tathaikamavaśeṣayeta .. 113 ..
2.12.d:
अन्नेन कुक्षेर्द्वावंशौ पानेनैकं प्रपूरयेत् ॥
आश्रयं पवनादीनां तथैकमवशेषयेत ॥ 113 ॥
2.12.m: One should fill two parts of the stomach with food and one with drink; / and one should leave one [part] empty as the seat of wind and the others.

2.12.s:
vyādhernidānasya tathā viparītamathauṣadham ..
kartavyametadevātra mayā sārdhaṃ prakīrtitam .. 114 ..
2.12.d:
व्याधेर्निदानस्य तथा विपरीतमथौषधम् ॥
कर्तव्यमेतदेवात्र मया सार्धं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 114 ॥
2.12.m: Medicine contrary to the disease and its cause / should be administered; this has been proclaimed by me together with [its practice].

2.12.s:
nābherūrdhvamadhaścaiva gudaśroṇyostathaiva ca ..
balāsapittavātānāṃ dehe sthānaṃ prakīrtitam .. 115 ..
2.12.d:
नाभेरूर्ध्वमधश्चैव गुदश्रोण्योस्तथैव च ॥
बलासपित्तवातानां देहे स्थानं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 115 ॥
2.12.m: Above the navel, below it, and at the anus and pelvis / are proclaimed the seats of phlegm, bile, and wind in the body.

2.12.s:
tathāpi sarvagā ete dehe vāyurviśeṣataḥ ..
dehasya madhye hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ tu manasaḥ smṛtam .. 116 ..
2.12.d:
तथापि सर्वगा एते देहे वायुर्विशेषतः ॥
देहस्य मध्ये हृदयं स्थानं तु मनसः स्मृतम् ॥ 116 ॥
2.12.m: Nevertheless, these move everywhere in the body, especially wind. / In the middle of the body is the heart, which is known as the seat of the mind.

2.12.s:
kṛśolpakeśaścapalo bahuvāgviṣamānalaḥ ..
vyomagaśca tathā svapne vātaprakṛtirucyate .. 117 ..
2.12.d:
कृशोल्पकेशश्चपलो बहुवाग्विषमानलः ॥
व्योमगश्च तथा स्वप्ने वातप्रकृतिरुच्यते ॥ 117 ॥
2.12.m: Emaciated, with sparse hair, unsteady, talkative, with irregular digestive fire, / and flying in the sky in dreams—such a person is said to be of wind constitution.

2.12.s:
akālapalitaḥ krodhī prasvedī madhurapriyaḥ ..
svapne ca dīptimatprekṣī pittaprakṛtirucyate .. 118 ..
2.12.d:
अकालपलितः क्रोधी प्रस्वेदी मधुरप्रियः ॥
स्वप्ने च दीप्तिमत्प्रेक्षी पित्तप्रकृतिरुच्यते ॥ 118 ॥
2.12.m: Prematurely grey, prone to anger, sweating profusely, fond of sweets, / and seeing luminous objects in dreams—such a person is said to be of bile constitution.

2.12.s:
dṛḍhāṅgaḥ sthiracittaśca suprajaḥ sthiramūrdhajaḥ ..
śuklāmbudarśau svapne ca kaphaprakṛtiko naraḥ .. 119 ..
2.12.d:
दृढाङ्गः स्थिरचित्तश्च सुप्रजः स्थिरमूर्धजः ॥
शुक्लाम्बुदर्शौ स्वप्ने च कफप्रकृतिको नरः ॥ 119 ॥
2.12.m: With firm limbs, steady mind, good offspring, steady hair on the head, / and seeing white clouds in dreams—such a man is of phlegm constitution.

2.12.s:
tāmasā rājasāścaiva sāttvikāśca tathā smṛtāḥ ..
mānuṣā bhṛguśārdūla vātapittakaphādhikāḥ .. 2.56.120 ..
2.12.d:
तामसा राजसाश्चैव सात्त्विकाश्च तथा स्मृताः ॥
मानुषा भृगुशार्दूल वातपित्तकफाधिकाः ॥ 2.56.120 ॥
2.12.m: Men dominated by wind, bile, and phlegm, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, / are regarded respectively as tāmasic, rājasic, and sāttvic.

2.12.s:
rūkṣaśītavyavāyādhvaguru karma pravartate ..
kadannabhojanādvāyurdehe śokācca kupyati .. 121 ..
2.12.d:
रूक्षशीतव्यवायाध्वगुरु कर्म प्रवर्तते ॥
कदन्नभोजनाद्वायुर्देहे शोकाच्च कुप्यति ॥ 121 ॥
2.12.m: Wind is aggravated in the body through dry and cold [things], sexual intercourse, walking, heavy exertion, / eating inferior food, and from grief.

2.12.s:
vidāhināṃ tathoṣṇānāmuccairadhvaniṣeviṇām ..
pittaṃ prakopamāyāti bhayena ca tathā dvija .. 122 ..
2.12.d:
विदाहिनां तथोष्णानामुच्चैरध्वनिषेविणाम् ॥
पित्तं प्रकोपमायाति भयेन च तथा द्विज ॥ 122 ॥
2.12.m: In those who indulge in foods that cause a burning sensation, in hot foods, and in loud speaking or walking on roads, / bile becomes aggravated, and likewise from fear, O twice-born.

2.12.s:
atyaṃbupānaviṣamabhojināṃ bhuvi śāyinām ..
śleṣmā prakopamāyāti tathā ye cālpabhojanāḥ .. 123 ..
2.12.d:
अत्यंबुपानविषमभोजिनां भुवि शायिनाम् ॥
श्लेष्मा प्रकोपमायाति तथा ये चाल्पभोजनाः ॥ 123 ॥
2.12.m: In those who drink excessive water, eat irregular meals, sleep on the ground, / and also in those who eat too little, phlegm becomes aggravated.

2.12.s:
vātapittakaphotthāni sarvarogāṇi dehinām ..
lakṣayellakṣaṇaṃ vidvāñśamayettadanantaram .. 124 ..
2.12.d:
वातपित्तकफोत्थानि सर्वरोगाणि देहिनाम् ॥
लक्षयेल्लक्षणं विद्वाञ्शमयेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥ 124 ॥
2.12.m: All diseases of embodied beings arise from wind, bile, and phlegm; / the wise one should observe the symptom and pacify it immediately thereafter.

2.12.s:
asthibhaṅgaḥ kaṣāyitvamāsye śuṣkāsyatā tathā ..
jṛṃbhaṇaṃ lomaharṣaśca vātikavyādhilakṣaṇam .. 125 ..
2.12.d:
अस्थिभङ्गः कषायित्वमास्ये शुष्कास्यता तथा ॥
जृंभणं लोमहर्षश्च वातिकव्याधिलक्षणम् ॥ 125 ॥
2.12.m: A feeling of broken bones, astringent taste in the mouth, dryness of the mouth, / yawning, and horripilation—these are the symptoms of a wind disease.

2.12.s:
nakhanetraśirāṇāṃ ca pītatā kaṭutā mukhe ...
tṛṣṇā dāho'mlatā caiva pittavyādhinidarśanam ... 126 ..
2.12.d:
नखनेत्रशिराणां च पीतता कटुता मुखे ॥।
तृष्णा दाहोऽम्लता चैव पित्तव्याधिनिदर्शनम् ॥। 126 ॥
2.12.m: Yellowness of the nails, eyes, and veins, bitterness in the mouth, / thirst, burning sensation, and sourness—these are the indication of a bile disease.

2.12.s:
ālasyaṃ ca prasekaśca gurutā madhurāsyatā ..
uṣṇābhilāṣitā ceti ślaiṣmikaṃ vyādhi lakṣaṇam .. 127 ..
2.12.d:
आलस्यं च प्रसेकश्च गुरुता मधुरास्यता ॥
उष्णाभिलाषिता चेति श्लैष्मिकं व्याधि लक्षणम् ॥ 127 ॥
2.12.m: Lethargy, salivation, heaviness, sweetness in the mouth, / and desire for warmth—such is the symptom of a phlegm disease.

2.12.s:
snigdhoṣṇamannaṃ sasukhā ca śayyā mano'nukūlāḥ suhṛdaḥ kathāśca ..
abhyañjanaṃ cāpyatitailapānaṃ vātaprakopapraśamāya dṛṣṭam ... .. 128 ..
2.12.d:
स्निग्धोष्णमन्नं ससुखा च शय्या मनोऽनुकूलाः सुहृदः कथाश्च ॥
अभ्यञ्जनं चाप्यतितैलपानं वातप्रकोपप्रशमाय दृष्टम् ॥॥। 128 ॥
2.12.m: Unctuous and warm food, a comfortable bed, agreeable friends and conversation, / anointment, and the copious drinking of oil are prescribed for the pacification of aggravated wind.

2.12.s:
sarāṃsi vāpyaḥ saritaḥ suśītāścandrāṃśavaścandanapaṅkalepāḥ ..
saṃsevitenāśu śamaṃ prayāti vilāsamagryaṃ manasaḥ praharṣāt .. 129 ..
2.12.d:
सरांसि वाप्यः सरितः सुशीताश्चन्द्रांशवश्चन्दनपङ्कलेपाः ॥
संसेवितेनाशु शमं प्रयाति विलासमग्र्यं मनसः प्रहर्षात् ॥ 129 ॥
2.12.m: Lakes, ponds, pleasantly cool rivers, moonbeams, and smearing with sandalwood paste— / through the enjoyment of these, [aggravated bile] quickly subsides, along with excellent diversion due to delight of the mind.

2.12.s:
sarvāmayārtipraśamārthamekāṃ tvamoṣadhīṃ rāma nibodha guhyām..
bhaktiḥ prabhordevavarasya viṣṇoryā sarvakāmaiḥ puruṣaṃ yunakti .. 2.56.130 .. ..
2.57
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
ārogyakaraṇaṃ nāma dvitīyā pratipattathā ..
ārogyadaṃ vrataṃ caiva vaiṣṇavaṃ kathayasva me .. 1 ..
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
dhaniṣṭhāsu mahābhāga yajamānapurohitau ...
upoṣya vāruṇaṃ snānaṃ yajamānasya kārayet .. 2 ..
kṛtvā kumbhaśataṃ sāgraṃ śaṃkhamuktāphalodakaiḥ ..
bhadrāsanopaviṣṭastaiḥ snātaścaivāhatāmbaraḥ .. 3 ...
keśavaṃ vāruṇaṃ candraṃ nakṣatraṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā ..
pūjayetprayato rāma gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ .. 4 ..

devatānāṃ yathoktānāṃ kurvīta havanaṃ tathā .. 5 ..

gurave vāsasī deye rasakumbhaṃ ca kāñcanam.. 6 ..
2.12.d:
सर्वामयार्तिप्रशमार्थमेकां त्वमोषधीं राम निबोध गुह्याम्॥
भक्तिः प्रभोर्देववरस्य विष्णोर्या सर्वकामैः पुरुषं युनक्ति ॥ 2.56.130 ॥ ॥
2.57
॥ राम उवाच ॥ ॥
आरोग्यकरणं नाम द्वितीया प्रतिपत्तथा ॥
आरोग्यदं व्रतं चैव वैष्णवं कथयस्व मे ॥ 1 ॥
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
धनिष्ठासु महाभाग यजमानपुरोहितौ ॥।
उपोष्य वारुणं स्नानं यजमानस्य कारयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
कृत्वा कुम्भशतं साग्रं शंखमुक्ताफलोदकैः ॥
भद्रासनोपविष्टस्तैः स्नातश्चैवाहताम्बरः ॥ 3 ॥।
केशवं वारुणं चन्द्रं नक्षत्रं वारुणं तथा ॥
पूजयेत्प्रयतो राम गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥ 4 ॥
धूपदीपनमस्कारैस्तथा चैवान्नसम्पदा ॥
देवतानां यथोक्तानां कुर्वीत हवनं तथा ॥ 5 ॥
सर्वौषधैस्तथाज्येन यथाशक्ति विधानतः ॥
गुरवे वाससी देये रसकुम्भं च काञ्चनम्॥ 6 ॥
2.12.m:
Learn from me, O Rāma, one secret remedy for pacifying the pain of all illnesses: / devotion to the Lord, the supreme god Viṣṇu, which unites a man with all desires.
2.57
Rāma said:
Tell me, indeed, the health-bestowing rite named "[Health-]Producer", as well as the Pratipad [and] Dvitīyā [rites],
and the Vaiṣṇava vow that bestows health. (1)
Puṣkara said:
When [the moon is in] Dhaniṣṭhā, O highly fortunate one, the patron and the priest,
having fasted, should cause the Vāruṇa bath to be performed for the patron. (2)
Having prepared fully a hundred jars with water [containing] conches and pearls,
seated on an auspicious seat, bathed with them and wearing unwashed [new] garments, (3)
controlled [in mind], O Rāma, he should worship Keśava, Vāruṇa, the moon, and likewise the asterism related to Varuṇa,
with perfumes, garlands, and unguents, (4)
with incenses, lamps, and prostrations, and likewise with an abundance of food.
In the same manner, he should perform an oblation to the aforesaid deities, (5)
with all medicinal herbs and with clarified butter, according to ability and rule.
Two garments should be given to the guru, as well as a jar of fluid and gold. (6)

2.12.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ pradātavyā vittaśaktyā ca dakṣiṇā ..
śamīśālmalijaiḥ patraivaṃśāgreṇa tathaiva ca .. 7 ..

śākāni haritaṃ mālyaṃ sarvasasyāni vāsasī ..
varuṇāyāśu nikṣipya gandhairdhūpairnivedayet ..8 ..

rogāḥ samastāḥ praśamaṃ prayānti baddhastathā mokṣamavāpnuyācca .. 9 .. ..
2.58
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
pauṣaśukladvitīyāyāṃ gavāṃ śṛṅgodakena tu ..
snātvā śuklāmbaro bhūtvā sūryestaṃ samupāgate .. 1 ..

2.12.d:
ब्राह्मणानां प्रदातव्या वित्तशक्त्या च दक्षिणा ॥
शमीशाल्मलिजैः पत्रैवंशाग्रेण तथैव च ॥ 7 ॥
त्रिवृतस्तु बलिः कार्यः सर्वरोगविनाशनः ॥
शाकानि हरितं माल्यं सर्वसस्यानि वाससी ॥
वरुणायाशु निक्षिप्य गन्धैर्धूपैर्निवेदयेत् ॥8 ॥
अलङ्घ्यमानस्य हि वारुणं तं स्नानेन दानेन कृतेन सम्यक् ॥
रोगाः समस्ताः प्रशमं प्रयान्ति बद्धस्तथा मोक्षमवाप्नुयाच्च ॥ 9 ॥ ॥
2.58
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
पौषशुक्लद्वितीयायां गवां शृङ्गोदकेन तु ॥
स्नात्वा शुक्लाम्बरो भूत्वा सूर्येस्तं समुपागते ॥ 1 ॥
बालेन्दोः पूजनं कृत्वा गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥
धूपदीपनमस्कारैस्तथा चैवान्नसम्पदा ॥ 2 ॥
दध्ना च परमान्नेन गुडेन लवणेन च ॥
पूजनैर्ब्राह्मणानां च पूजयित्वा निशाकरम् ॥ 3 ॥
यावदस्तं न यातीन्दुस्तावदेव समाचरेत् ॥
आहारं गोरसप्रायमधःशायी निशं नयेत् ॥ 4 ॥
2.12.m:
And a sacrificial fee should be given to the brahmins according to one's wealth.
With leaves born of the śamī and the śālmali, and likewise with the tip of a bamboo, (7)
a three-fold offering should be made, which destroys all diseases.
Vegetables, a fresh green garland, all kinds of grain, and two garments—
having quickly cast [them] down for Varuṇa, he should present them with perfumes and incenses. (8)
For of one who does not transgress that Vāruṇa [rite],
through the bath and the gift performed properly,
all diseases go to cessation,
and one who is bound would obtain release. (9)
2.58
Puṣkara said:
On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa,
having bathed with water from the horns of cows, becoming clad in white garments when the sun has set, (1)
having performed worship of the young moon with perfumes, garlands, and unguents,
with incenses, lamps, and prostrations, and likewise with an abundance of food, (2)
with curds, fine rice-pudding, molasses, and salt,
and through acts of worship of brahmins, having worshipped the maker of the night [the moon], (3)
he should consume food consisting predominantly of cow-milk products only as long as the moon does not set;
[then] sleeping on the ground, he should pass the night. (4)

2.12.s:
tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe saumyamāse dvijottama ..
bālendoḥ pūjanaṃ kṛtvā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca pūjanam .. 5 ..
vāsasī rasakumbhaṃ ca kāñcanaṃ ca dvijātaye ..
dattvā ca pūjayitvā ca vratapāraṅgato bhavet .. 6 ..
vratenānena dharmajña rogamevaṃ vyapohati ..
sarvasaukhyaṃ tathā dravyaṃ puṣṭiṃ ca manujottama .. 7 ..
kāmaṃ samāpnotyathavaikamiṣṭaṃ yena vratenātha samastadharmam ..
abhyāsatastasya samastakāmānnaraḥ samāpnoti kimatra citram .. 8 .. ..
2.59
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
saṃvatsarāvasāne tu pañcadaśyāmupoṣitaḥ ..
pūjayedbhāskaraṃ devaṃ varṇakaiḥ kamale kṛte .. 1 ..
śuklena gandhamālyena candanena sitena ca ..
tathā kūrmeṇa dhūpena ghṛtadīpena bhārgava .. 2 ..
apūpaiḥ saikatairdadhnā paramānnena bhūriṇā ..
odanena ca śuklena sitālavaṇasarpiṣā .. 3 ..
2.12.d:
ततः संवत्सरे पूर्णे सौम्यमासे द्विजोत्तम ॥
बालेन्दोः पूजनं कृत्वा ब्राह्मणानां च पूजनम् ॥ 5 ॥
वाससी रसकुम्भं च काञ्चनं च द्विजातये ॥
दत्त्वा च पूजयित्वा च व्रतपारङ्गतो भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
व्रतेनानेन धर्मज्ञ रोगमेवं व्यपोहति ॥
सर्वसौख्यं तथा द्रव्यं पुष्टिं च मनुजोत्तम ॥ 7 ॥
कामं समाप्नोत्यथवैकमिष्टं येन व्रतेनाथ समस्तधर्मम् ॥
अभ्यासतस्तस्य समस्तकामान्नरः समाप्नोति किमत्र चित्रम् ॥ 8 ॥ ॥
2.59
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
संवत्सरावसाने तु पञ्चदश्यामुपोषितः ॥
पूजयेद्भास्करं देवं वर्णकैः कमले कृते ॥ 1 ॥
शुक्लेन गन्धमाल्येन चन्दनेन सितेन च ॥
तथा कूर्मेण धूपेन घृतदीपेन भार्गव ॥ 2 ॥
अपूपैः सैकतैर्दध्ना परमान्नेन भूरिणा ॥
ओदनेन च शुक्लेन सितालवणसर्पिषा ॥ 3 ॥
2.12.m:
Then, when a year is completed, in the month of Saumya [Mārgaśīrṣa], O best of the twice-born,
having performed worship of the young moon and worship of brahmins, (5)
having given two garments, a jar of fluid, and gold to a twice-born man,
and having worshipped him, he becomes one who has crossed to the other side of the vow. (6)
By this vow, O knower of dharma, one dispels disease in this manner;
likewise [he obtains] all happiness, wealth, and nourishment, O best of men. (7)
He attains his desire, or [even] that one cherished [goal], through which vow he then [attains] all dharma;
from its practice a man attains all desires—what wonder is there in this? (8)
2.59
Puṣkara said:
At the end of the year, having fasted on the fifteenth day,
one should worship god Bhāskara [the Sun] on a lotus made with pigments, (1)
with white perfume and garland, and with white sandalwood,
likewise with tortoise-incense and a lamp with clarified butter, O descendant of Bhṛgu, (2)
with pastries, with sugar, with curds, with abundant fine rice-pudding,
and with white boiled rice, with white salt and clarified butter, (3)

2.12.s:
kṣīreṇa ca phalaiḥ śuklairvahnibrāhmaṇatarpaṇaiḥ ..
pūjayitvā jagaddhāma dinabhāge caturthake .. 4 ..
āhāraṃ prathamaṃ kuryātsaghṛtaṃ manujottamaḥ ..
rasaṃ ca manujaśreṣṭha ghṛtahīnaṃ vivarjayet .. 5 ..
bhuktvā ca sakṛdevānnaṃ nāhāraṃ samupācaret ..
pānīyapānaṃ kurvīta brāhmaṇānumate punaḥ .. 6 ..
saṃvatsaramidaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kṛtvā trayodaśam ..
pūjanaṃ devadevasya tasminnahani bhārgava .. 7 ..
samāpayedvrataṃ puṇyaṃ rāma kumbhaṃ dvijātaye ..
sahiraṇyaṃ savastraṃ ca tathā dadyāddvijottama .. 8 ..
vratenānena dharmajña rogameva vyapohati ..
ārogyamāpnoti gatiṃ tathāgryāṃ yaśastathāgryaṃ vipulāṃśca bhogān ..
vratena samyakpuruṣo dhanārthī sampūjayedyaśca jagatpradhānam .. 9 ..
2.60
puṣkara uvāca ..
śuklapakṣāvasāne tu yadrāma dinapañcakam ..
tatra sampūjayedviṣṇuṃ vidhinā yena taṃ śṛṇu .. 1 ..
2.12.d:
क्षीरेण च फलैः शुक्लैर्वह्निब्राह्मणतर्पणैः ॥
पूजयित्वा जगद्धाम दिनभागे चतुर्थके ॥ 4 ॥
आहारं प्रथमं कुर्यात्सघृतं मनुजोत्तमः ॥
रसं च मनुजश्रेष्ठ घृतहीनं विवर्जयेत् ॥ 5 ॥
भुक्त्वा च सकृदेवान्नं नाहारं समुपाचरेत् ॥
पानीयपानं कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणानुमते पुनः ॥ 6 ॥
संवत्सरमिदं कृत्वा ततः कृत्वा त्रयोदशम् ॥
पूजनं देवदेवस्य तस्मिन्नहनि भार्गव ॥ 7 ॥
समापयेद्व्रतं पुण्यं राम कुम्भं द्विजातये ॥
सहिरण्यं सवस्त्रं च तथा दद्याद्द्विजोत्तम ॥ 8 ॥
व्रतेनानेन धर्मज्ञ रोगमेव व्यपोहति ॥
आरोग्यमाप्नोति गतिं तथाग्र्यां यशस्तथाग्र्यं विपुलांश्च भोगान् ॥
व्रतेन सम्यक्पुरुषो धनार्थी सम्पूजयेद्यश्च जगत्प्रधानम् ॥ 9 ॥
2.60
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
शुक्लपक्षावसाने तु यद्राम दिनपञ्चकम् ॥
तत्र सम्पूजयेद्विष्णुं विधिना येन तं शृणु ॥ 1 ॥
2.12.m:
and with milk, with white fruits, and with satisfactions offered to the fire and brahmins.
Having worshipped the abode of the universe in the fourth part of the day, (4)
the best of men should take his first meal, accompanied by clarified butter;
and, O best of men, he should avoid juice that is devoid of clarified butter. (5)
And having eaten food only once, he should not take [further] food;
he may drink water again, with the permission of a brahmin. (6)
Having done this for a year, and having then performed the thirteenth
worship of the god of gods on that day, O descendant of Bhṛgu, (7)
he should complete the holy vow, O Rāma;
likewise, he should give a jar with gold and with cloth to a twice-born man, O best of the twice-born. (8)
By this vow, O knower of dharma, he dispels disease;
he obtains health, likewise the highest state, the highest fame, and extensive enjoyments—
the man desirous of wealth who properly worships the principal [deity] of the universe with this vow. (9)
2.60
Puṣkara said:
During the five days that [occur] at the end of the bright fortnight, O Rāma,
one should worship Viṣṇu there; listen to the rule by which [one should do so]: (1)

gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhisarpistathaiva ca .
ekaikena caretsnānamekādaśyādiṣu kramāta .. 2 ..

2.12.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधिसर्पिस्तथैव च ।
एकैकेन चरेत्स्नानमेकादश्यादिषु क्रमात ॥ 2 ॥
कौपताडागनादेयैः पद्मिनीसारसैर्जलैः ॥
कर्तव्यं क्रमशः स्नानं स्नातः सम्पूजयेद्धरिम् ॥ 3 ॥
तैलमिक्षुरसं क्षौद्रं क्षीरं सर्पिश्च भार्गव ॥
स्नपयेद्देवदेवस्य कर्तव्यं स्याद्दिनक्रमात् ॥ 4 ॥
कालागुरुमुशीरं च तथा जातीफलं द्विज ॥
कर्पूरं चन्दनं चैव कल्पयेदनुलेपने ॥5॥
कुसुमेष्वम्बुजातेषु गन्धवत्सु सितेषु च ॥
एकैकं कल्पयेज्जातिं श्रद्धया दिवसक्रमात् ॥6॥
कृष्णा गौरी तथा ताम्रा कपिला च सिता तथा॥ ॥
या धेनुस्तद्घृतं देयं दीपार्थं दिवसक्रमात् ॥ 7
माषमुद्गकलापानां चणकस्य तिलस्य च ॥
भक्ष्याणि विनिवेद्यानि तथैव दिवसक्रमात् ॥ 8 ॥
फाणितं च गुडं चैव तथा मत्स्यण्डिका शुभा ॥
खण्डं च शर्करां चैव क्रमशो विनिवेदयेत् ॥9 ॥
2.12.m:
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, and likewise clarified butter—
one should perform a bath with each one in succession on the days beginning with the eleventh. (2)
A bath should be performed in succession with water from wells, tanks, and rivers, and water from lotus-lakes;
having bathed, he should worship Hari. (3)
Oil, sugarcane juice, honey, milk, and clarified butter, O descendant of Bhṛgu—
the bathing of the god of gods should be performed in the order of the days. (4)
Black agallochum, uśīra, and likewise nutmeg, O twice-born one,
camphor and sandalwood he should provide for the unguent. (5)
Among fragrant and white water-born flowers,
he should provide one single variety with faith in the order of the days. (6)
Black, fair, copper-coloured, tawny, and white—
the clarified butter of such a cow is to be given for the lamp in the order of the days. (7)
Eatables made of black gram, green gram, peas, chickpeas, and sesame
are to be offered in the very same order of the days. (8)
Boiled sugarcane juice, molasses, auspicious candied sugar,
raw sugar, and refined sugar he should present in succession. (9)

2.12.d:
क्षीरवृक्षस्य समिधस्तथा दूर्वास्तिलानपि ॥।
सिद्धार्थकान्यथाज्यं च भावयेद्दिवसक्रमात् ॥ 2.60.10 ॥
अनिरुद्धाय देवाय प्रद्युम्नाय तथैव च ॥
संकर्षणाय देवाय वासुदेवाय चाप्यथ ॥ 11 ॥
नाम्ना तु जुहुयाद्वह्निं प्रणवेनान्तिमेऽहनि ॥
अयः सीसं तथा ताम्रं रजतं कनकं तथा ॥ 12 ॥
दक्षिणार्थं प्रदातव्यं द्विजेभ्यो दिवसक्रमात् ॥
नक्तं च गोरसप्रायं भोक्तव्यं तैलवर्जितम् ॥ 13 ॥
भूशोधनं च कर्तव्यं देवस्य पुरतस्तथा ॥
गीतवाद्यस्तवैश्चैव पूजयेद्दिनपञ्चकम् ॥ 14 ॥
एवं संवत्सरं कृत्वा सर्वान्रोगान्व्यपोहति ॥
ग्रहणे च व्रतस्यास्य न कालनियमः स्मृतः ॥ 15 ॥
नित्याभ्यासेन चैवास्य विष्णुलोके महीयते॥
व्रतं श्रेष्ठमिदं प्रोक्तं मया ते भृगुनन्दन ॥ 16 ॥
2.12.m:
Sacrificial sticks of a milky tree, dūrvā grass, and sesame seeds,
white mustard seeds, and clarified butter he should employ in the order of the days. (10)
To Lord Aniruddha, and likewise to Pradyumna,
to Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa, and also to Vāsudeva— (11)
by name he should offer into the fire, and with the praṇava on the final day.
Iron, lead, copper, silver, and gold— (12)
must be given as a sacrificial fee to twice-born [brahmins] in order of the days. / And at night, one should eat what consists mostly of dairy, free of oil.
And purification of the ground should be performed before the deity; / one should worship for five days with song, instrumental music, and hymns of praise.
Doing thus for a year, one dispels all diseases; / and in taking up this observance, no restriction of time is recorded.
And through its constant practice, one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. / This excellent observance has been proclaimed to you by me, O joy of the Bhṛgus.

2.12.d:
धन्यं यशस्यं रिपुनाशकारि सौभाग्यदं पापहरं पवित्रम् ॥
आयुष्यमग्र्यं सुगतिप्रदं च व्रतोत्तमं विघ्नविनाशनं च ॥17॥
2.12.m: It brings fortune, brings renown, causes the destruction of enemies, bestows good luck, removes sin, is purifying, / promotes long life, is foremost, grants a good destination, is the best of observances, and destroys obstacles.
